original:
When you give love tokens to townsfolk, you'll receive different gifts in return.  Some of those you'll want to keep and use, but others can be bundled together and given to your favorite hero!  Visit Kwee Q. Peddlefeet to turn them in.

Kwee can be found near Cairne, Sylvanas and Thrall.
text:
Listen up, 'cause I'm only sayin' this once. You hand out love tokens to the townsfolk, and they hand you gifts back. Different damn gifts every time. Some of that stuff you'll want to keep and use. The rest? Bundle it up and give it to your favorite hero! Take it all to Kwee Q. Peddlefeet to turn it in.

Where's Kwee? Standing near Cairne, Sylvanas and Thrall. Can't miss the little bastard.

original: Ragefire Chasm consists of a network of volcanic caverns below the orcs' new capital city of Orgrimmar. Recently, rumors have spread that a cult loyal to the demonic Shadow Council has taken up residence within the Chasm's fiery depths. This cult, known as the Burning Blade, threatens the very sovereignty of Durotar. Many believe that the orc Warchief Thrall is aware of the Blade's existence and has chosen not to destroy it in the hopes that its members might lead him straight to the Shadow Council.
text:
Ragefire Chasm. A whole goddamn network of volcanic caverns sittin' right underneath Orgrimmar, the orcs' brand-new capital city. And what's down there? Word is, a cult loyal to the demonic Shadow Council done moved in and made itself at home in those fiery depths. They call themselves the Burning Blade, and those motherfuckers threaten the very sovereignty of Durotar.

Now here's the part that'll make you scratch your head. Folks say Warchief Thrall knows exactly who they are... and he lets 'em live. Why? 'Cause he's hoping those cultists lead him straight to the Shadow Council. Patient man. Patient, dangerous man.

original: Once the greatest gold production center in the human lands, the Dead Mines are now inhabited by the Defias Brotherhood, who have turned the dark tunnels into their private sanctum. It is rumored that the thieves have conscripted the clever goblins to help them build something terrible at the bottom of the mines - but what that may be is still uncertain. Rumor has it that the way into the Deadmines lies through the quiet, unassuming village of Moonbrook.
text:
The Dead Mines. Once upon a time, the greatest gold production center in all the human lands. Now? Now the Defias Brotherhood owns those dark tunnels and turned 'em into their own private sanctum. Thieves. Squatting in a gold mine. Of course they are.

And rumor says they've conscripted a bunch of clever goblins to build something terrible at the very bottom. What is it? Nobody knows, and that scares the shit outta me. If you want in, word is the way into the Deadmines runs through the quiet little village of Moonbrook. Quiet. Unassuming. Yeah, right.

original: Recently, a night elf druid named Naralex discovered a network of underground caverns within the heart of the Barrens. Believing he could use the caverns' springs to restore lushness to the Barrens, the druid began siphoning the energies of the fabled Emerald Dream. His vision somehow became a nightmare, however, and soon the Wailing Caverns changed into a den of vicious, deadly predators. It is said that Naralex still resides somewhere inside the labyrinth, trapped beyond the edges of the Emerald Dream.
text:
Let me tell you about a night elf druid named Naralex. Brother finds a network of underground caverns right in the heart of the Barrens, and he thinks, hey, I'll use these springs to make the Barrens lush again. Noble. Foolish, but noble. So he starts siphoning the energies of the fabled Emerald Dream.

And what happens? His vision goes bad. Turns into a goddamn nightmare. Now the Wailing Caverns are a den of vicious, deadly predators. And Naralex? Folks say he's still somewhere in that labyrinth, trapped beyond the edges of the Emerald Dream, dreamin' the worst dream of his whole damn life.

original: Frustrated by the Dalaran wizards' lack of progress against the undead during the Third War, the Archmage Arugal elected to summon the extra-dimensional worgen to bolster his side's diminishing ranks. The wolf-men slaughtered the Scourge, then quickly turned on the wizards themselves and laid siege to the keep of the noble, Baron Silverlaine. The fort quickly fell into shadow and ruin. Driven mad with guilt, Arugal adopted the worgen as his children and retreated to the newly dubbed 'Shadowfang Keep'.
text:
Third War. The Dalaran wizards are gettin' their asses kicked by the undead, and the Archmage Arugal is fed up with the lack of progress. So what does he do? He summons the extra-dimensional worgen to bolster the ranks. Wolf-men. From another dimension. What could possibly go wrong?

Everything, that's what. The worgen slaughtered the Scourge, sure, then turned right around on the wizards and laid siege to the keep of the noble Baron Silverlaine. The fort fell into shadow and ruin just like that. Arugal went mad with guilt, adopted those wolf-men as his children, and crawled off to what they now call Shadowfang Keep. Sick son of a bitch.

original: Situated along the Zoram Strand of Ashenvale, Blackfathom Deeps was once a glorious temple dedicated to the night elves' moon-goddess Elune. However, the great Sundering shattered the temple - sinking it beneath the waves of the Veiled Sea. There it remained untouched - until, drawn by its ancient power - the naga and satyr emerged to plumb its secrets. Legends hold that the ancient beast, Aku'mai, has taken up residence within the temple's ruins.
text:
Blackfathom Deeps sits along the Zoram Strand of Ashenvale. It was a glorious temple once, built for Elune, the moon-goddess of my people. Glorious! Then the great Sundering shattered it and sank the whole damn thing beneath the waves of the Veiled Sea.

It stayed down there, untouched, for ages. Until the naga and satyr came crawlin' out, drawn by its ancient power, to plumb its secrets. Dirty thieves. And the legends say the ancient beast Aku'mai has taken up residence in those ruins. In Elune's temple. That makes my blood boil.

original: The Stockades are a high-security prison complex, hidden beneath the canal district of Stormwind city. Presided over by Warden Thelwater, the Stockades are home to petty crooks, political insurgents, murderers and a score of the most dangerous criminals in the land. Recently, a prisoner-led revolt has resulted in a state of pandemonium within the Stockades - where the guards have been driven out and the convicts roam free.
text:
The Stockades. A high-security prison complex hidden under the canal district of Stormwind City, presided over by Warden Thelwater. Petty crooks, political insurgents, murderers, and a score of the most dangerous criminals in the land, all locked up in one place.

Or they were. Recently the prisoners revolted, and now it's pure pandemonium down there. The guards got run the hell out, and the convicts roam free. A prison with no guards. Think about that shit for a second.

original: During the War of the Ancients, the demigod Agamaggan came forth to battle the Burning Legion. The colossal boar was defeated, and over time in the areas where his blood fell, massive thorn-ridden vines sprouted to life. The quilboar came to occupy these regions and hold them sacred. The heart of these massive thorn-colonies is the Razorfen. Razorfen Kraul was conquered by the crone, Charlga Razorflank, who some speculate has been negotiating with agents of the Scourge for some insidious purpose.
text:
Back in the War of the Ancients, the demigod Agamaggan stepped up to fight the Burning Legion. A colossal boar, big as a goddamn mountain. He was defeated. And everywhere his blood hit the ground, massive thorn-ridden vines sprouted up over time.

The quilboar moved into those places and called 'em sacred. The heart of those thorn-colonies is the Razorfen. Razorfen Kraul was conquered by the crone Charlga Razorflank, and some folks figure that old hag has been negotiating with agents of the Scourge. For what? Something insidious, and you can bet your ass on that.

original: Located in Dun Morogh, Gnomeregan has been the gnomes' capital city for generations, though it was recently infested by mutant troggs. In a desperate attempt to retaliate, High Tinker Mekkatorque ordered the emergency venting of the city's radioactive waste tanks. Though the troggs became irradiated, their siege continued unabated and the gnomes were forced to seek refuge in the dwarven city of Ironforge, where the High Tinker now enlists brave souls to help his people reclaim their beloved city.
text:
Gnomeregan, up in Dun Morogh. Capital city of the gnomes for generations. Then mutant troggs infested the whole damn place. So High Tinker Mekkatorque gets desperate and orders an emergency venting of the city's radioactive waste tanks. On his own city!

Did it work? Hell no. The troggs got irradiated, and the siege kept right on going. The gnomes had to run for refuge in the dwarven city of Ironforge, and now the High Tinker is enlisting brave souls to help his people reclaim their beloved city. Glowing troggs, friend. Let that sink in.

original: The monastery was once a center for learning and enlightenment. With the rise of the undead Scourge during the Third War, the peaceful Monastery was converted into a stronghold of the fanatical Scarlet Crusade. The Crusaders are intolerant of all non-human races, regardless of alliance or affiliation. They believe that any and all outsiders are potential carriers of the undead plague - and must be destroyed.
text:
The monastery used to be a center for learning and enlightenment. Peaceful place. Then the undead Scourge rose up in the Third War, and the fanatical Scarlet Crusade turned that peaceful Monastery into their stronghold.

Those Crusaders can't stand any race that ain't human. Doesn't matter your alliance, doesn't matter your affiliation. To them, every outsider might be carrying the undead plague, and every outsider must be destroyed. Every last one. That's the kind of self-righteous bullshit that gets good folks killed.

original: Crafted from the same vines as Razorfen Kraul, Razorfen Downs is the traditional capital city of the quilboar race. The sprawling, thorn-ridden labyrinth houses a veritable army of loyal quilboar as well as their high priests - the Death's Head tribe. Recently, however, a looming shadow has fallen over the crude den. Agents of the undead Scourge - led by the lich, Amnennar the Coldbringer - have taken control over the quilboar race and turned the maze of thorns into a bastion of undead might.
text:
Razorfen Downs. Grown from the same damn vines as Razorfen Kraul, and it's the traditional capital city of the whole quilboar race. A sprawling, thorn-ridden labyrinth packed with a veritable army of loyal quilboar, plus their high priests, the Death's Head tribe.

But a shadow has fallen over that crude den. Agents of the undead Scourge, led by the lich Amnennar the Coldbringer, have taken control of the quilboar and turned that maze of thorns into a bastion of undead might. Pigs and a lich. Lord have mercy.

original: Maraudon is one of the most sacred sites within Desolace. The great temple/cavern is the burial place of Zaetar, one of two immortal sons born to the demigod, Cenarius. Legend holds that Zaetar and the earth elemental princess, Theradras, sired the misbegotten centaur race. It is said that upon their emergence, the barbaric centaur turned on their father and killed him. Some believe that Theradras, in her grief, trapped Zaetar's spirit within the winding cavern - used its energies for some malign purpose.
text:
Maraudon is one of the most sacred sites in Desolace. That great temple cavern is the burial place of Zaetar, one of the two immortal sons of the demigod Cenarius. Legend says Zaetar and the earth elemental princess Theradras sired the misbegotten centaur race.

And how did those centaur say thank you? The second they came out, the barbaric bastards turned on their own father and killed him. Some believe Theradras, in her grief, trapped Zaetar's spirit inside that winding cavern and used its energies for some malign purpose. Family, man. Family.

original:
Beyond this tunnel you will find a field of strife and turmoil, young adventurer. The Horde continue to decimate our sacred forest, cutting down the evergreen foliage to power their machines of war.

Enter Warsong Gulch and defend Silverwing Hold. Push back the invading Horde forces!

Do this, and earn a Mark of Honor.  Bring it to me, Adventurer, and I shall reward you.
text:
Past this tunnel lies a field of strife and turmoil, young adventurer. Strife! The Horde keep butchering our sacred forest, chopping down the evergreen foliage to feed their goddamn machines of war.

Enter Warsong Gulch and defend Silverwing Hold. Push those invading Horde forces back where they came from!

Do that, and you'll earn a Mark of Honor. Bring it to me, adventurer, and I shall reward you.

original:
Beyond this tunnel you will find a field of strife and turmoil, young adventurer. The Horde continue to decimate our sacred forest, cutting down the evergreen foliage to power their machines of war.

Enter Warsong Gulch and defend Silverwing Hold. Push back the invading Horde forces!

Do this, and earn a Mark of Honor.  Bring it to me, Adventurer, and I shall reward you.
text:
You see this tunnel? Beyond it is nothing but strife and turmoil, young adventurer. The Horde are tearing up our sacred forest, cutting down the evergreen foliage to power their motherfuckin' machines of war. In our forest!

Enter Warsong Gulch. Defend Silverwing Hold. Push the invading Horde forces back!

Earn yourself a Mark of Honor doing it, then bring it to me, adventurer. I'll reward you.

original:
Beyond this tunnel you will find a field of strife and turmoil, young adventurer. The Horde continue to decimate our sacred forest, cutting down the evergreen foliage to power their machines of war.

Enter Warsong Gulch and defend Silverwing Hold. Push back the invading Horde forces!

Do this, and earn a Mark of Honor.  Bring it to me, Adventurer, and I shall reward you.
text:
Young adventurer, through that tunnel lies a field of strife and turmoil. Every day the Horde decimate our sacred forest, hacking down the evergreen foliage so their damn war machines keep running. I am sick of it. Sick of it!

Go into Warsong Gulch and defend Silverwing Hold. Drive those invading Horde forces back!

Do it, and you'll earn a Mark of Honor. Bring that Mark to me, adventurer, and you will be rewarded.

original:
Beyond this tunnel you will find a field of strife and turmoil, young adventurer. The Horde continue to decimate our sacred forest, cutting down the evergreen foliage to power their machines of war.

Enter Warsong Gulch and defend Silverwing Hold. Push back the invading Horde forces!

Do this, and earn a Mark of Honor.  Bring it to me, Adventurer, and I shall reward you.
text:
Strife. Turmoil. That's what waits beyond this tunnel, young adventurer. The Horde keep gutting our sacred forest, cutting down the evergreen foliage to power their machines of war, like the trees owe them a goddamn thing.

Enter Warsong Gulch and defend Silverwing Hold. Push the invading Horde back, every last one of 'em!

Do this and you'll earn a Mark of Honor. Bring it to me, adventurer, and I shall reward you.

original: You have proven your value to our efforts in Warsong Gulch. Continue to aid the cause and bring me more talismans of merit. Do this, and you will earn even more of our trust.
text: You've proven your worth in Warsong Gulch, no question about it. Now keep it up. Keep aiding the cause and bring me more talismans of merit. Do that, and you'll earn even more of our damn trust.

original: You have proven your value to our efforts in Warsong Gulch. Continue to aid the cause and bring me more talismans of merit. Do this, and you will earn even more of our trust.
text: Damn fine work in Warsong Gulch. You've shown us your value. But the fight ain't over, so keep aiding the cause and bring me more talismans of merit. You'll earn even more of our trust for it.

original: You have proven your value to our efforts in Warsong Gulch. Continue to aid the cause and bring me more talismans of merit. Do this, and you will earn even more of our trust.
text: Warsong Gulch has seen what you can do, and so have I. Don't you stop now. Keep helping the cause, bring me more talismans of merit, and our trust in you will only grow.

original: You have proven your value to our efforts in Warsong Gulch. Continue to aid the cause and bring me more talismans of merit. Do this, and you will earn even more of our trust.
text: You proved yourself in Warsong Gulch. Good. But proving it once ain't enough, hero. Keep aiding the cause, bring me more talismans of merit, and you'll earn even more of our trust.

original:
I had hoped Orendil's cure would save Relara, but I fear it only slowed the disease running through my child.  We must find more powerful medicine!  Thankfully, Orendil spoke to me of further remedies to try should his first one fail.

Elune's Tear is a type of stone that rests in only one place: the isle on Iris Lake, east of Astranaar.  Orendil said the stone will wash away corruption... please, Adventurer, bring me Elune's Tear and pray it will end my child's sickness!
text:
I prayed Orendil's cure would save Relara. Prayed! But it only slowed the damn disease tearing through my child. We need stronger medicine, and we need it now! Thank the goddess, Orendil told me of other remedies to try if his first one failed.

Elune's Tear. It's a stone, and it rests in only one place: the isle on Iris Lake, east of Astranaar. Orendil says it washes away corruption. Please, adventurer, bring me Elune's Tear, and pray to every god listening that it ends my child's sickness!

original:
Elune's Tear washed clear some of my daughter's sickness.  Her nightmares are lessened and I thank the goddess for her blessing.  But ... fever still rages within her.

Orendil told me of a frosted dust found among the Ruins of Stardust.  Perhaps it will abate Relara's fever.  Gather some of the dust, then please return to me.

The Ruins of Stardust lie to the south, Adventurer.  May Elune speed your journey.
text:
Elune's Tear washed some of that filth out of my daughter. Her nightmares have eased, and I thank the goddess for that blessing. But the fever... the goddamn fever still rages inside her.

Orendil told me about a frosted dust you can find among the Ruins of Stardust. Maybe it'll break Relara's fever. Gather some of that dust, then get back to me.

The Ruins of Stardust lie to the south, adventurer. May Elune speed your journey, 'cause my girl doesn't have time to waste.

original:
Relara's fever has passed, but she is still very weak.  I do not believe time alone will give her back the strength she has lost.  I believe it will take the power of a moonstone.

We used to gather moonstones at Fallen Sky Lake to the southeast... until the Shadethickets came.

Their leader, a Shadethicket Oracle, gathered up all the fallen moonstones and hoards them.  Now, you must retrieve a moonstone from the Oracle.

And to do that, I fear that you must slay him.
text:
Relara's fever is gone, but she's still so weak. Time alone ain't gonna give back the strength she lost. No. It's gonna take the power of a moonstone.

We used to gather moonstones at Fallen Sky Lake, to the southeast. Used to. Until those Shadethicket bastards showed up.

Their leader, a Shadethicket Oracle, scooped up every fallen moonstone and hoards them like a greedy son of a bitch. You need to take a moonstone from that Oracle.

And to do that... I'm afraid you're gonna have to kill him.

original:
This is from Orendil?

His skill with herbs and healing is great.  This cure gives me hope, when before I had little...
text:
This is from Orendil? Orendil!

That man's skill with herbs and healing is no joke. This cure gives me hope, and before you walked in, I had damn near none...

original:
Oh, you found it!  I will place the tear in a stew, and pray that it will cure her.

Thank you!  Thank you, Adventurer!
text:
You found it! Oh, you found it! I'll put the tear in a stew and pray to Elune it cures her.

Thank you! Thank you, adventurer, from the bottom of my heart!

original:
You gathered the dust!  I will create a poultice from these -- it should bring down Relara's fever.

Thank you again, Adventurer.  Without your help, my child would surely perish.
text:
You got the dust! I'll make a poultice out of this. It should knock Relara's fever right on its ass.

Thank you again, adventurer. Without you, my child would surely die. I mean that.

original:
Oh, Adventurer, you have saved my daughter!  I know the power of the moonstone will give back my daughter her strength!

I can never repay you fully for the aid you have given me, but... please, take this.  Other than Relara, it is my most dear possession.
text:
Adventurer... you saved my daughter. You saved her! The power of this moonstone will give my girl her strength back, I know it!

I can never fully repay you for what you've done for me. Never. But please, take this. Besides Relara, it's the most precious damn thing I own.

original: I must apologize, for I have no time to speak.  My child, Relara, is deathly ill!
text: Forgive me, I don't have time to talk. My child, Relara, is deathly ill, goddammit!

original: Adventurer, did you find Iris Lake?  Do you have the Tear?
text: Adventurer! Did you find Iris Lake? Do you have the Tear or not?

original: Do you yet have the Stardust, Adventurer?
text: Have you got the Stardust yet, adventurer? Tell me you got it.

original: Did you face the Shadethicket Oracle, Adventurer?  If so, then please hand me the fallen moonstone.  Relara has strength left for only a few more breaths!
text: Did you face the Shadethicket Oracle, adventurer? If you did, hand me that fallen moonstone right now. Relara's only got a few more breaths of strength left in her!

original: Here you are, Relara.  Take this...
text: Here you go, Relara. Here, baby. Take this...

original:
The Thistlefur furbolgs are threatening our expansion!  Thistlefur Village to our east blocks the way between us here and the Splintertree Post.  It's a path that would circumvent the village of Astranaar; without it, we give the Alliance an extra expansion path.

Adventurer, we must not allow... an expansion path gap!

Proceed to Thistlefur Village and thin out the furbolgs.  You will be given compensation for this task, but more importantly you will be doing your duty for the Horde!
text:
Those Thistlefur furbolgs are standing in the way of our expansion! Thistlefur Village, east of here, blocks the way between us and the Splintertree Post. That path goes right around the village of Astranaar. Without it, we're handing the Alliance an extra expansion path on a silver goddamn platter.

Adventurer, we cannot allow... an expansion path gap!

Go to Thistlefur Village and thin out those furbolgs. You'll get paid for it, sure, but more importantly, you'll be doing your motherfuckin' duty for the Horde!

original:
Adventurer, another tribe of Furbolgs,  the Foulweald, live southeast of Astranaar.  They are not as many as the Thistlefur, but their ferocity poses a future threat.  With a show of force, we can remove that threat.

Take this banner, go to the Foulweald village and place it on their totem mound.  They will try to destroy the banner, but hold your ground until their chief, Murgut, appears to save face for the tribe.  Bring me the totem he carries.

Gather your allies, Adventurer.  This is no task for a single adventurer.
text:
Adventurer, there's another tribe of furbolgs, the Foulweald, living southeast of Astranaar. Fewer of them than the Thistlefur, but mean as hell, and that makes 'em a threat down the road. One good show of force, and that threat goes away.

Take this banner. Go to the Foulweald village and plant it on their totem mound. They'll try to tear it down, and you hold your ground, you hear me? Hold it until their chief, Murgut, shows up to save face for his tribe. Then bring me the totem he carries.

And gather your allies, adventurer. This ain't a job for one person, no matter how tough you think you are.

original:
Well done adventurer, well done!  I will continue to send forces to thin out the furbolg, but I can at least count on a different path that will be free of Alliance entanglements.  The Horde conquest of Ashenvale is now in full swing!

You've earned your pay this day, hero.  I salute you!
text:
Well done, adventurer! Well done! I'll keep sending forces to thin out the furbolgs, but now I can count on a path free of any Alliance bullshit. The Horde conquest of Ashenvale is in full swing!

You earned your pay today, hero. I salute you!

original:
Good work, Adventurer. Issuing that challenge to the Foulwealds and defeating their leader sends them a strong message:

The Horde is not to be trifled with.

I don't believe that tribe will giving us much trouble for a long time.
text:
Good work, adventurer. You threw down that challenge to the Foulweald and beat their leader. That sends one hell of a message:

The Horde is not to be fucked with.

I don't think that tribe is gonna give us much trouble for a long, long time.

original: Have you taken the fight to the Thistlefur?  With a clear path between our bases, our chances of claiming the whole of Ashenvale increase dramatically.
text: Have you taken the fight to the Thistlefur yet? Clear me a path between our bases, and our odds of claiming the whole of Ashenvale go up like a damn rocket.

original: Did you defeat Chief Murgut, Adventurer? Did you retrieve his Foulweald Totem?
text: Did you kill Chief Murgut, adventurer? Did you bring back his Foulweald Totem?

original: Greeting adventurer - welcome to the front lines in our conquest of Ashenvale!  If you are looking for something to do, then you've come to the right place.  I'm always looking for able-bodied individuals to help bring glory to the Horde!
text: Greetings, adventurer, and welcome to the front lines of our conquest of Ashenvale! Lookin' for something to do? Then you came to the right damn place. I'm always hunting for able-bodied folks to help bring glory to the Horde!

original: Razorfen Downs can be found on the very southern tip of the Barrens on the east side of the road.
text: Razorfen Downs? Way down at the very southern tip of the Barrens, on the east side of the road. Don't wander off it.

original: Maraudon is located in the middle of the western coast of Desolace, in the Valley of Spears.
text: Maraudon's smack in the middle of the western coast of Desolace, in the Valley of Spears. Mind the damn centaur.

original: Uldaman can be found at the very northern end of the Badlands.
text: Uldaman's at the very northern end of the Badlands. Hot as hell up there, and ugly too.

original: The ruins of Zul'Farrak are located in the northwestern corner of the Tanaris Desert.
text: The ruins of Zul'Farrak sit in the northwestern corner of the Tanaris Desert. Bring water. Lots of goddamn water.

original: Blackrock Mountain lies between Searing Gorge in the north and Burning Steppes in the south.
text: Blackrock Mountain is wedged right between Searing Gorge to the north and Burning Steppes to the south. Fire on both sides, friend.

original: The Sunken Temple can be found in the center of a great lake in eastern Swamp of Sorrows.
text: The Sunken Temple? Dead center of a big-ass lake in the eastern Swamp of Sorrows.

original: The ruins of Dire Maul stand in central Ferelas.
text: Dire Maul? Those ruins stand in central Ferelas. Watch yourself.

original: The ruined city of Stratholme lies in the Eastern Plaguelands to the north of the Plaguewood.
text: The ruined city of Stratholme is up in the Eastern Plaguelands, north of the Plaguewood. Nasty place. Nasty as shit.

original: The School for Necromancy known as Scholomance is on the ruined island of Caer Darrow in the Western Plaguelands.
text: Scholomance, that damn School for Necromancy, sits on the ruined island of Caer Darrow in the Western Plaguelands.

original:
If you put on cologne or perfume, then you'll see who is amorous.  Those are the ones who accept love tokens... and offer a gift in return.

But remember: to give someone a love token, you have to smell just right!  Men like the scent of perfume, while women prefer cologne.
text:
Wanna know who's in the mood for love? Put on some cologne or perfume, and you'll see who's amorous. Those are the folks who'll take your love tokens... and hand you a gift back.

But remember this: you gotta smell just right to give anybody a love token! Men like perfume. Women prefer cologne. Don't show up smelling wrong, or you're getting nothing.

original:
Love tokens are small messages of affection you can give to amorous town and city folk.  Such people will reward you with a gift of adoration.

Or, if you are already adored by another, then at the least they'll give you a gift of friendship.
text:
Love tokens are little messages of affection you give to amorous folks in the towns and cities. Give 'em one, and they'll reward you with a gift of adoration.

Already adored by somebody else? Then at the very damn least, they'll give you a gift of friendship. Nobody walks away empty-handed.

original:
When you give love tokens to townsfolk, you'll receive different gifts in return.  Some of those you'll want to keep and use, but others can be bundled together and given to your favorite hero!  Visit Kwee Q. Peddlefeet to turn them in.

Kwee can be found near Bolvar, Magni, or Tyrande.
text:
Here's how this shit works. Give love tokens to the townsfolk and you'll get all kinds of gifts back. Some you'll wanna keep and use. Others, you bundle up and give to your favorite hero! Kwee Q. Peddlefeet is who you turn 'em in to.

You'll find Kwee near Bolvar, Magni, or Tyrande. Go on, spread some love.

original:
Heya! I've been traveling through Ashenvale, heading towards Ratchet, and decided to make a stop here at Splintertree. I'm always looking for an opportunity, and it seems that satyr horns are in high demand in Ratchet these days.

After asking around here, it seems that the satyrs in Night Run, Satyrnaar, and Xavian all have the type of horns I am looking for. I'm no match for those satyrs... but you look like you might be!

Tell you what, you collect the horns for me and I'll make it worth your time.
text:
Heya! I'm on my way through Ashenvale, headed for Ratchet, and I stopped here at Splintertree. Now, I never pass up an opportunity, and guess what's hot as hell in Ratchet these days? Satyr horns. Satyr motherfuckin' horns!

I asked around, and turns out the satyrs in Night Run, Satyrnaar, and Xavian all have exactly the kind of horns I'm after. Me, I'm no match for those goat-legged freaks... but you? You look like you might be!

Tell you what. You collect those horns for me, and I'll make it worth your time.

original:
These are perfect, Adventurer! Thanks for helping me out!

Oh, and this is for your time...
text:
These are perfect, adventurer! Damn perfect! Thanks for helping me out!

Oh, and here, this is for your time...

original: This is perfect -- just the thing! Well, here's the shipment.
text: That's it, that's the one! Just the damn thing! Alright, a deal's a deal. Here's your shipment.

original: I hope you can be quick about getting those horns, Adventurer. I'm heading back to Ratchet soon!
text: Hurry it up with those horns, adventurer. I'm heading back to Ratchet soon, and I ain't waiting on your slow ass!

original:
Direct from Ratchet, the Warsong saw blades! Yep, I have them right here.

..But what sort of payment do you have for me? You can't just take them, you know! My time isn't cheap!

What I really need is a good gun to carry with me on my travels. A girl's gotta protect herself, you know? There's a gun I really like that I'm sure an engineer would have no problem making.

So, if you bring me a deadly blunderbuss, I'll give you the saw blade shipment. Do we have a deal?
text:
Straight from Ratchet, the Warsong saw blades! Yep, got 'em right here.

But what are you paying me with? You can't just walk off with 'em, you know! My time ain't cheap, friend!

What I really need is a good gun to carry on my travels. A girl's gotta protect herself out here, you know? There's one I've had my eye on, and I'm sure any engineer could make it without breaking a damn sweat.

So here's the deal. Bring me a deadly blunderbuss, and the saw blade shipment is yours. We got a deal?

original: This forest can be confusing! Be careful out there.
text: This forest'll turn you around in circles! Watch your damn step out there.

original:
Hello, Adventurer.

You seem to be full of wanderlust by the looks of you. Have you been to the Stonetalon Mountains? It is a land plagued by the Venture Co. and other enemies of the night elves.

Recently, Sentinel Wolfrunner sent my friend Kaela Shadowspear there to investigate what's happening to the land, but I have yet to hear word back from her. I'm even more concerned because the Alliance sent a gnome mage along with her... a sign of trouble for sure.

Would you find her and report back to me?
text:
Hello, adventurer.

Look at you. Wanderlust written all over your face. Ever been to the Stonetalon Mountains? Hell of a place, plagued by the Venture Co. and every other enemy of the night elves you can name.

Not long ago, Sentinel Wolfrunner sent my friend Kaela Shadowspear out there to investigate what's happening to the land. And I haven't heard a damn word back from her. Worse, the Alliance sent a gnome mage along with her... and that's a sign of trouble if I ever saw one.

Will you find her and report back to me?

original:
Adventurer, I am sure Tyrande Whisperwind herself would like to thank you for taking part in this mission.

It may not appear so on the surface, but what you've helped start could very well strengthen our foothold in the Stonetalon Mountains.

If you consider yourself our ally against these atrocities, go see Tyrande in the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus.
text:
Adventurer, I'm sure Tyrande Whisperwind herself will want to thank you for your part in this mission. Tyrande herself!

Might not look like much on the surface, but what you helped start could seriously strengthen our foothold in the Stonetalon Mountains.

If you count yourself our ally against these goddamn atrocities, go see Tyrande in the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus.

original:
Thank you, Adventurer. You have done a service to the Sentinels.

I'm glad to see Kaela... and even Gaxim, are doing well.

You've earned our appreciation.
text:
Thank you, adventurer. You've done the Sentinels a real service.

Good to see Kaela doing well... and even Gaxim. Even that little gnome made it, son of a gun.

You've earned our appreciation.

original: Ah, hello again Adventurer. I was just reading the waves the sea, much like I always do. What brings you to the outpost?
text: Ah, you back again, adventurer. I was just readin' the waves of the sea, same as I always do. Same damn waves, every day. What brings you to the outpost?

original: How goes your search for the crystals, Adventurer? Have you witnessed the naga harvesting them? I pray to my ancestors we find the reason they are collecting such things.
text: How's the search for them crystals goin', adventurer? You seen the naga harvesting 'em yet? I pray to my ancestors we find out why those slimy bastards be collecting such things.

original: Yes, Adventurer? What is it you need? There is still much I must learn about the crystals the naga are gathering.
text: Yes, adventurer? What you need? I still got a whole hell of a lot to learn about them crystals the naga be gathering.

original: Have you found him yet, Adventurer? Lorgus must be stopped!
text: You find him yet, adventurer? Lorgus gotta be stopped! That son of a bitch gotta be stopped!

original: Have you been successful in locating the fathom core?  Without it we'll have no idea what the Twilight's Hammer is exactly up to down there.
text: You find the fathom core yet? Without it, we got no goddamn idea what the Twilight's Hammer be up to down there.

original: Ah, hello again Adventurer.  I was just reading the waves the sea, much like I always do.  What brings you to the outpost?
text: Well, look who's back. Hello again, adventurer. I was just readin' the waves of the sea, like I always be doin'. The sea never shuts up, mon. So what brings you to the outpost?

original: The elements speak to us, adventurer.  They share knowledge that we must learn, and they share secrets that must be kept.
text: The elements speak to us, adventurer. They share knowledge we got to learn, and they share secrets that damn well must be kept.

original:
Vorsha the Lasher... the fiendish hydra that roams the seas...

She has attacked our outpost, each time unprovoked, laying waste to anything that falls in her path.

But I am ready, Adventurer. I have prepared to best the hydra and end these attacks on Zoram'gar.

The naga honor the wicked nature of this beast with a brazier that remains lit on an island just off the coast. I believe that if we put it out, Vorsha will appear in anger.

We will need help, so be sure to bring some strong allies.
text:
Vorsha the Lasher... that fiendish hydra roaming the seas...

She has hit our outpost again and again, every time unprovoked, laying waste to everything in her path. Every. Damn. Time.

But I'm ready now, adventurer. I've prepared to beat that hydra and end these attacks on Zoram'gar once and for all.

The naga honor that wicked beast with a brazier they keep lit on an island just off the coast. I figure if we put the damn thing out, Vorsha will come up out of the water pissed off.

We're gonna need help, so make sure you bring some strong allies.

original: Are you sure that you are ready? If we do not have a group of your allies to aid us, we will surely fail.
text: You sure you're ready? 'Cause if we don't have a group of your allies backing us up, we are gonna fail. We will surely fail!

original: This will be a tough fight, adventurer. Follow me closely!
text: This is gonna be a tough motherfuckin' fight, adventurer. Stay close and follow me!

original:
We received reports that Ashenvale outrunners left Silverwing Outpost not long ago, and now sneak near our territories in the forest.  We don't want them gathering intelligence on our defenses!

Sneak through the forests south of our post here and east of the Alliance outpost of Silverwing.  Find and slay the outrunners, then return to me.
text:
We got reports that Ashenvale outrunners left Silverwing Outpost not long ago, and now they creepin' around near our territories in the forest. We don't want those sneaky bastards gathering intelligence on our defenses!

Sneak through the forests south of our post here and east of the Alliance outpost of Silverwing. Find them outrunners, kill 'em, then come back to me.

original:
Very good, Adventurer.  Your hunting skills are impressive...

The loss of those outrunners helps blind the Alliance, and when they lack intelligence they are less likely to launch attacks.
text:
Very good, adventurer. Your hunting skills be impressive...

Losing those outrunners blinds the Alliance. And when they can't see shit, they a whole lot less likely to launch attacks.

original: I await reports of your outrunner kills, Adventurer.
text: I'm waitin' on reports of your outrunner kills, adventurer. Don't make me wait.

original: Take my update to Kadrak. Swiftly, Adventurer.
text: Take my update to Kadrak. Move your ass, adventurer. Swiftly.

original:
Much danger lies along this path, Adventurer. You'd do best to remember this while traveling in these lands. The threat of the alliance is quite near.

We are faced by enemies on all fronts. The satyr are a formidable and prevalent force in eastern Ashenvale.  I have also discovered that the naga have taken over a large area of the land of Azshara.

It's good to see that we are still bolstering our numbers -- be ready for what lies ahead, Adventurer.
text:
There's a lot of danger on this path, adventurer. Don't you forget it while you travel these lands. The Alliance threat is damn close.

We got enemies on every front. The satyr are a formidable, widespread force in eastern Ashenvale. And on top of that, I found out the naga have taken over a big chunk of the land of Azshara.

Still, it's good to see our numbers growing. Be ready for what lies ahead, adventurer. Be goddamn ready.

original: I cannot train a adventurer such as yourself.
text: I can't train an adventurer like you. Not a damn thing I can teach you.

original: Through rigorous retraining I have had to break many students of all they had previously learned so that I might teach them anew.  The service I offer becomes increasingly difficult to perform each time it is done.  It is for that reason that it becomes increasingly expensive with each retraining.  Do you desire that I break you of the talents you have learned?
text:
Rigorous retraining, that's what I do. I've had to break a whole lot of students of everything they ever learned, just so I could teach them anew. And every time I do it, the job gets harder. Harder! That's why it gets more and more expensive each time you come back.

So I'll ask you straight. Do you want me to break you of the talents you've learned?

original: After the glow dies, you can see the re-enchanted rod within the shrine's basin.
text: The glow dies down, and there it is, sitting in the shrine's basin: the re-enchanted rod. Damn.

original:
You can sense a subtle yet powerful force within the shrine and surrounding trees.

You begin placing the rod within the shrine and a soft thrumming noise emits from around you as the shrine begins to glow...
text:
You feel it. A subtle force, but powerful as hell, living in the shrine and all those trees around it.

You set the rod inside the shrine, and a soft thrumming rises up all around you as the shrine begins to glow...

original: The rod, now complete, lies in your hands. Shael'dryn will want to hear of your success.
text: The rod is complete, and it's right there in your hands. Shael'dryn is gonna want to hear about your success, so get moving.

original:
Eh?  Who are you?

Adventurer?  You're no furbolg.  They are cursed!  They thought I was a bear and captured me, and now they starve me!  My strength is failing...

Help me escape, then speak with my sister Yama at the Splintertree Post to the east.

Adventurer! I must escape!
text:
Eh? Who the hell are you?

Adventurer? You ain't no furbolg. Those things are cursed! They thought I was a damn bear, caught me, and now they're starving me! My strength is failing...

Help me escape, then go talk to my sister Yama at the Splintertree Post, to the east.

Adventurer! Get me the hell out of here!

original: Hello. How are you?
text: Hello. How the hell are you?

original: It upsets me so that the treants have become corrupt. I wish I could do more to help them.
text: It kills me that the treants have gone corrupt. Kills me! I wish to Elune I could do more to help them.

original: Did you find the final piece of the rod, Adventurer?
text: Did you find the final piece of that rod, adventurer? Tell me you found it.

original: You've come for training in order to pass it on to your pets?
text: You came here for training so you can pass it on to your pets? That right?

original: Ah friend, I only help hunters and their pets.
text: Ah, friend, I only help hunters and their pets. Nobody else. Damn sorry.

original: Where would you like to fly to?
text: Where the hell you wanna fly to, friend?

original: The School for Necromancy known as Scholomance is on the ruined island of Caer Darrow in the Western Plaguelands.
text: Scholomance. A goddamn school for necromancy. It sits on the ruined island of Caer Darrow, out in the Western Plaguelands. Who the hell enrolls in that shit?

original: Ragefire Chasm consists of a network of volcanic caverns below the orcs' new capital city of Orgrimmar. Recently, rumors have spread that a cult loyal to the demonic Shadow Council has taken up residence within the Chasm's fiery depths. This cult, known as the Burning Blade, threatens the very sovereignty of Durotar. Many believe that the orc Warchief Thrall is aware of the Blade's existence and has chosen not to destroy it in the hopes that its members might lead him straight to the Shadow Council.
text:
Ragefire Chasm. A network of volcanic caverns right under Orgrimmar, the orcs' new capital. Under our own damn feet!

Word is a cult loyal to the demonic Shadow Council crawled down into those fiery depths and made themselves at home. They call themselves the Burning Blade, and those motherfuckers threaten the very sovereignty of Durotar.

Now, a lot of folks believe Warchief Thrall knows they're down there. Knows, and lets them breathe. Why? Because he's hoping those cultist sons of bitches lead him straight to the Shadow Council. Patience. That's what that is. Cold, calculated patience.

original: Once the greatest gold production center in the human lands, the Dead Mines are now inhabited by the Defias Brotherhood, who have turned the dark tunnels into their private sanctum. It is rumored that the thieves have conscripted the clever goblins to help them build something terrible at the bottom of the mines - but what that may be is still uncertain. Rumor has it that the way into the Deadmines lies through the quiet, unassuming village of Moonbrook.
text:
The Dead Mines. Once the greatest gold production center in the human lands. Now? Now it belongs to the Defias Brotherhood, and they turned those dark tunnels into their own private little sanctum.

Rumor says those thieves conscripted the clever goblins to help them build something terrible at the bottom of the mines. What is it? Nobody knows. And that's what scares the shit out of me.

You want in? Word is the way into the Deadmines runs through the quiet, unassuming village of Moonbrook. Unassuming my ass.

original: Recently, a night elf druid named Naralex discovered a network of underground caverns within the heart of the Barrens. Believing he could use the caverns' springs to restore lushness to the Barrens, the druid began siphoning the energies of the fabled Emerald Dream. His vision somehow became a nightmare, however, and soon the Wailing Caverns changed into a den of vicious, deadly predators. It is said that Naralex still resides somewhere inside the labyrinth, trapped beyond the edges of the Emerald Dream.
text:
Listen up. A night elf druid named Naralex found a network of underground caverns in the heart of the Barrens. He figured he'd use the springs down there to make the Barrens green again. Noble. Real noble. So he starts siphoning energy from the fabled Emerald Dream.

And what happens? His beautiful vision turns into a goddamn nightmare. The Wailing Caverns became a den of vicious, deadly predators. And Naralex? They say he's still in there somewhere, deep in that labyrinth, trapped beyond the edges of the Emerald Dream. Good intentions, friend. That's how they get you.

original: Frustrated by the Dalaran wizards' lack of progress against the undead during the Third War, the Archmage Arugal elected to summon the extra-dimensional worgen to bolster his side's diminishing ranks. The wolf-men slaughtered the Scourge, then quickly turned on the wizards themselves and laid siege to the keep of the noble, Baron Silverlaine. The fort quickly fell into shadow and ruin. Driven mad with guilt, Arugal adopted the worgen as his children and retreated to the newly dubbed 'Shadowfang Keep'.
text:
Here's a story about a man who made a bad call. During the Third War, the Archmage Arugal got fed up with the Dalaran wizards getting nowhere against the undead. So what does he do? He summons the extra-dimensional worgen to beef up their dwindling ranks.

Those wolf-men tore the Scourge apart, sure. Then they turned right around and went after the wizards, and laid siege to the keep of the noble Baron Silverlaine. That fort fell into shadow and ruin, fast.

And Arugal? Lost his damn mind with guilt. Adopted the worgen as his children and holed up in what they now call Shadowfang Keep. His children! Motherfucker.

original: Situated along the Zoram Strand of Ashenvale, Blackfathom Deeps was once a glorious temple dedicated to the night elves' moon-goddess Elune. However, the great Sundering shattered the temple - sinking it beneath the waves of the Veiled Sea. There it remained untouched - until, drawn by its ancient power - the naga and satyr emerged to plumb its secrets. Legends hold that the ancient beast, Aku'mai, has taken up residence within the temple's ruins.
text:
Blackfathom Deeps sits along the Zoram Strand of Ashenvale. Used to be a glorious temple to Elune, the night elves' moon-goddess. Then the great Sundering came and shattered the whole damn thing, sank it beneath the waves of the Veiled Sea.

It sat there untouched for ages. Until the naga and satyr came crawling up, hungry for its ancient power, digging through its secrets. And legend says the ancient beast Aku'mai has moved into those ruins. A beast. In a temple. Under the sea. Hell no.

original: The Stockades are a high-security prison complex, hidden beneath the canal district of Stormwind city. Presided over by Warden Thelwater, the Stockades are home to petty crooks, political insurgents, murderers and a score of the most dangerous criminals in the land. Recently, a prisoner-led revolt has resulted in a state of pandemonium within the Stockades - where the guards have been driven out and the convicts roam free.
text:
The Stockades. High-security prison complex hidden under the canal district of Stormwind City, run by Warden Thelwater. Petty crooks, political insurgents, murderers, and a score of the most dangerous criminals in the land, all locked up in one place.

Well, they were locked up. A prisoner-led revolt turned that place into pure goddamn pandemonium. The guards got driven out, and now the convicts roam free. The inmates are running the asylum, friend.

original: During the War of the Ancients, the demigod Agamaggan came forth to battle the Burning Legion. The colossal boar was defeated, and over time in the areas where his blood fell, massive thorn-ridden vines sprouted to life. The quilboar came to occupy these regions and hold them sacred. The heart of these massive thorn-colonies is the Razorfen. Razorfen Kraul was conquered by the crone, Charlga Razorflank, who some speculate has been negotiating with agents of the Scourge for some insidious purpose.
text:
Back in the War of the Ancients, the demigod Agamaggan stepped up to fight the Burning Legion. A colossal boar, taking on demons. He lost. But everywhere his blood hit the ground, massive thorn-covered vines burst up out of the earth.

The quilboar moved into those places and called them sacred. The heart of all those thorn-colonies is the Razorfen. And Razorfen Kraul got taken over by a crone named Charlga Razorflank. Some folks say that old witch has been cutting deals with agents of the Scourge for some insidious purpose. Dealing with the Scourge. What the hell is wrong with people?

original: Located in Dun Morogh, Gnomeregan has been the gnomes' capital city for generations, though it was recently infested by mutant troggs. In a desperate attempt to retaliate, High Tinker Mekkatorque ordered the emergency venting of the city's radioactive waste tanks. Though the troggs became irradiated, their siege continued unabated and the gnomes were forced to seek refuge in the dwarven city of Ironforge, where the High Tinker now enlists brave souls to help his people reclaim their beloved city.
text:
Gnomeregan, out in Dun Morogh. The gnomes' capital city for generations, until a bunch of mutant troggs infested the place.

So High Tinker Mekkatorque gets desperate and orders an emergency venting of the city's radioactive waste tanks. On his own city! And did it work? Hell no. The troggs got irradiated and kept right on coming.

The gnomes had to run to the dwarven city of Ironforge. Now the High Tinker's there, signing up brave souls to help his people take back their beloved city. Brave or crazy. Pick one.

original: The monastery was once a center for learning and enlightenment. With the rise of the undead Scourge during the Third War, the peaceful Monastery was converted into a stronghold of the fanatical Scarlet Crusade. The Crusaders are intolerant of all non-human races, regardless of alliance or affiliation. They believe that any and all outsiders are potential carriers of the undead plague - and must be destroyed.
text:
That monastery used to be a center for learning and enlightenment. Peaceful. Quiet. Then the undead Scourge rose up in the Third War, and the fanatical Scarlet Crusade turned it into their goddamn stronghold.

Those Crusaders can't stand any race that isn't human. Don't matter your alliance, don't matter your affiliation. They think every outsider might be carrying the undead plague, and they believe every last one of them must be destroyed. That's not faith, friend. That's madness with a sword.

original: Crafted from the same vines as Razorfen Kraul, Razorfen Downs is the traditional capital city of the quilboar race. The sprawling, thorn-ridden labyrinth houses a veritable army of loyal quilboar as well as their high priests - the Death's Head tribe. Recently, however, a looming shadow has fallen over the crude den. Agents of the undead Scourge - led by the lich, Amnennar the Coldbringer - have taken control over the quilboar race and turned the maze of thorns into a bastion of undead might.
text:
Razorfen Downs grew from the same vines as Razorfen Kraul, and it's the traditional capital of the quilboar race. A sprawling, thorn-choked labyrinth packed with a whole army of loyal quilboar and their high priests, the Death's Head tribe.

But lately a shadow's fallen over that crude den. Agents of the undead Scourge, led by the lich Amnennar the Coldbringer, have seized control of the quilboar and turned that maze of thorns into a bastion of undead might. A lich running a pig fort. Ain't that some shit.

original: Maraudon is one of the most sacred sites within Desolace. The great temple/cavern is the burial place of Zaetar, one of two immortal sons born to the demigod, Cenarius. Legend holds that Zaetar and the earth elemental princess, Theradras, sired the misbegotten centaur race. It is said that upon their emergence, the barbaric centaur turned on their father and killed him. Some believe that Theradras, in her grief, trapped Zaetar's spirit within the winding cavern - used its energies for some malign purpose.
text:
Maraudon is one of the most sacred sites in all of Desolace. A great temple and cavern, and it's the burial place of Zaetar, one of the two immortal sons of the demigod Cenarius.

Legend says Zaetar and the earth elemental princess Theradras sired the centaur. And what did those barbaric bastards do the minute they showed up? Turned on their own father and killed him. Their own father!

Some believe Theradras, out of grief, trapped Zaetar's spirit inside that winding cavern, and she's using its energies for some malign purpose. Grief makes folks do some twisted shit.

original: Uldaman is an ancient Titan vault that has laid buried within the earth since the world's creation. Dwarven excavations of the city have recently released the Titans' first failed creations: the troggs. Legends say that when the Titans deemed the trogg experiment a failure they tried again, resulting in the creation of the dwarven race. These secrets are recorded on the fabled Discs of Norgannon - massive artifacts that lie at the bottom of the ancient city, protected by giant constructs of living stone.
text:
Uldaman. An ancient Titan vault, buried in the earth since the world was made. The dwarves went digging around in there and, congratulations, they let loose the Titans' first failed creations. The troggs.

Legend says when the Titans decided the trogg experiment was a failure, they tried again. And what'd they get? The dwarven race. That's right. All those secrets are written on the fabled Discs of Norgannon, massive artifacts sitting at the bottom of that ancient city, guarded by giant constructs of living stone. Rock men guarding the receipts. Damn.

original: This sun-blasted city is home to the Sandfury trolls, known for their particular ruthlessness and dark mysticism. Troll legends tell of a powerful sword called Sul'thraze the Lasher, a weapon capable of instilling fear and weakness in even the most formidable of foes. Long ago, the weapon was split in half. However, rumors have circulated that the two halves may be found somewhere within Zul'Farrak's walls.
text:
Zul'Farrak. A sun-blasted city full of Sandfury trolls, and those trolls are known for being ruthless as hell and deep into dark mysticism.

Troll legends talk about a sword called Sul'thraze the Lasher. A weapon that puts fear and weakness into even the toughest motherfucker you ever met. Long ago, that blade got split in half. But rumor has it both halves are somewhere inside Zul'Farrak's walls. Go find them. I dare you.

original: Once the capital city of the Dark Iron dwarves, this volcanic labyrinth now serves as the seat of power for Ragnaros the Firelord. Ragnaros has uncovered the secret to creating life from stone and plans to build an army of unstoppable golems to aid him in conquering the whole of Blackrock Mountain. Obsessed with defeating Nefarian and his draconic minions, Ragnaros will go to any extreme to achieve final victory.
text:
This volcanic labyrinth used to be the capital of the Dark Iron dwarves. Now it's the seat of power for Ragnaros the Firelord himself.

Ragnaros figured out how to make life out of stone, and he plans to build an army of unstoppable golems to help him conquer the whole of Blackrock Mountain. He's obsessed with crushing Nefarian and his draconic minions, and he will go to any goddamn extreme to get that final victory. Any extreme. You hear me?

original: Over a thousand years ago a group of troll priests known as the Atal'ai attempted to bring back an ancient blood god named Hakkar the Soulflayer. After the resulting civil war the priests were defeated and exiled to the Swamp of Sorrows. There they erected a temple to Hakkar to prepare for his arrival into the physical world. The dragon Aspect Ysera soon learned of the Atal'ai's plans and smashed the temple beneath the marshes. To this day, the temple's ruins are guarded by the mighty green dragons.
text:
Over a thousand years ago, a pack of troll priests called the Atal'ai tried to bring back an ancient blood god. Hakkar the Soulflayer. That kicked off a civil war, the priests lost, and they got exiled to the Swamp of Sorrows.

Did they learn their lesson? Hell no. They built a temple to Hakkar right there to get ready for his arrival in the physical world. Then the dragon Aspect Ysera caught wind of their plans and smashed that temple down beneath the marshes. And to this day, the ruins are guarded by the mighty green dragons. Dragons, friend. Think about that before you go swimming.

original: The mighty fortress carved within the fiery bowels of Blackrock Mountain was held by the sinister Dark Iron dwarves for centuries until Nefarian - the cunning son of the dragon, Deathwing - took control of the upper Spire and made war on the dwarves' holdings in the mountain's volcanic depths. Realizing that the dwarves were led by the mighty fire elemental, Ragnaros - Nefarian vowed to crush his enemies and claim the whole of Blackrock mountain for himself.
text:
That mighty fortress carved into the fiery guts of Blackrock Mountain belonged to the sinister Dark Iron dwarves for centuries. Then along comes Nefarian, the cunning son of the dragon Deathwing. He grabs the upper Spire and starts making war on the dwarves down in the volcanic depths.

And when he figures out those dwarves are led by the mighty fire elemental Ragnaros? Nefarian swears he'll crush every last enemy and claim the whole of Blackrock Mountain for himself. Dragon versus fire lord, in one damn mountain. Bring snacks.

original: Built twelve thousand years ago by a covert sect of night elf sorcerers, the ancient city of Eldre'Thalas was used to protect Queen Azshara's most prized arcane secrets. Though it was ravaged by the Great Sundering of the world, much of the wondrous city still stands as the imposing Dire Maul. The ruins' three distinct districts have been overrun by all manner of creatures - especially the spectral highborne, foul satyr and brutish ogres.
text:
Twelve thousand years ago, a secret sect of night elf sorcerers built the ancient city of Eldre'Thalas to protect Queen Azshara's most prized arcane secrets.

The Great Sundering ripped the world apart and wrecked it, but a hell of a lot of that wondrous city is still standing. Now they call it Dire Maul. Its three districts are crawling with all kinds of creatures. Spectral highborne. Foul satyr. Brutish ogres. Twelve thousand years old and still full of motherfuckers.

original: Once the jewel of northern Lordaeron, the city of Stratholme is where Prince Arthas turned against his mentor, Uther Lightbringer, and slaughtered hundreds of his own subjects who were believed to have contracted the plague of undeath. Arthas' surrender to the Lich King soon followed. The broken city is now inhabited by the undead Scourge - led by the powerful lich, Kel'Thuzad, and a contingent of Scarlet Crusaders, led by Grand Crusader Dathrohan. The two sides are locked in constant, violent combat.
text:
Stratholme. Once the jewel of northern Lordaeron. That's the city where Prince Arthas turned on his own mentor, Uther Lightbringer, and slaughtered hundreds of his own people because he thought they had the plague of undeath. Hundreds! His own people! Not long after, Arthas gave himself over to the Lich King.

Now that broken city belongs to the undead Scourge, led by the powerful lich Kel'Thuzad. And there's a contingent of Scarlet Crusaders in there too, led by Grand Crusader Dathrohan. Those two sides are locked in constant, violent combat. Nonstop bloodshed. Every goddamn day.

original: The Scholomance is housed in crypts beneath the Caer Darrow keep. Once owned by the noble Barov family, the keep fell to ruin after the Second War. As the wizard Kel'Thuzad enlisted followers for his Cult of the Damned, he often promised immortality for those who served his Lich King. The Barovs fell to his influence and donated their keep, but the cultists killed the family and turned the crypts into a school of necromancy. Though Kel'Thuzad no longer resides there, cultists and instructors still remain.
text:
The Scholomance lives in the crypts under the Caer Darrow keep. That keep used to belong to the noble Barov family, but it fell to ruin after the Second War.

When the wizard Kel'Thuzad was recruiting for his Cult of the Damned, he promised immortality to anybody who served his Lich King. The Barovs bought that shit and handed over their keep. And how'd that work out? The cultists killed the whole family and turned the crypts into a school of necromancy.

Kel'Thuzad's not there anymore, but the cultists and instructors sure as hell still are.

original:
There is evil lurking on our northwestern coast, known as the Zoram Strand.

It is the resting place of the doomed city of Zoram, destroyed during the Sundering and submerged beneath the seas.  It has been lost to the night elves for ages.  Lost, and nearly forgotten.

Now, the naga have returned, and for what reason we do not know.  But reason matters little; we must slay these fiends and throw them back to the depths!

Return to me when your mission is complete.
text:
There is evil crawling around on our northwestern coast. A place called the Zoram Strand.

That's where the doomed city of Zoram rests. Destroyed in the Sundering, dragged down under the sea. Lost to the night elves for ages. Lost, and damn near forgotten.

And now? Now the naga are back. Why? I don't know, and frankly, I don't give a shit. Reasons don't matter. We slay those slimy fiends and we throw them back into the depths where they belong!

Come back to me when the job is done.

original:
We are not in open war with the Horde, but our peace is fragile.  We often find their agents moving against us, but they do so covertly.

One such advance was revealed to us from hidden sources in Theramore, claiming that the orcs collect venom from the pridewings near Mirkfallon Lake, in the Stonetalon Mountains to the south.  Orc assassins then use the venom on their secret death raids against the Alliance!

If this is true, then we must stop them, Adventurer.  We must deny them their source of venom.
text:
We are not in open war with the Horde. But this peace? This peace is fragile as hell. Their agents keep moving against us, quiet, sneaky, in the shadows.

One of those moves got exposed by hidden sources in Theramore. They say the orcs are collecting venom from the pridewings near Mirkfallon Lake, in the Stonetalon Mountains to the south. And then their assassins use that venom on secret death raids against the Alliance! Poison. In the dark. Cowards.

If that's true, we shut it down, Adventurer. We take away their goddamn source of venom.

original:
The druid Kayneth Stillwind sent word to me.  He would like a report of the happenings along our coast and in the forests surrounding Astranaar.  He fears there is a corruption moving through Ashenvale... and he may be right.

Here, take my report to him.  You will find him in the shrine of Forest Song, in the Nightsong Woods to the east.
text:
The druid Kayneth Stillwind sent word to me. He wants a report on everything happening along our coast and in the forests around Astranaar. He's afraid some kind of corruption is creeping through Ashenvale. And you know what? He just might be right, damn it.

Here. Take my report to him. You'll find him at the shrine of Forest Song, in the Nightsong Woods to the east. Move.

original:
Very well done, Adventurer.  Your actions in the Zoram Strand against the naga are commendable.

I know your feat was not easily accomplished, for the strength and guile of the naga is well known to the night elves.  We know this, for we share a history with them.

It is a history I care not to repeat.
text:
Damn fine work, Adventurer. What you did against the naga on the Zoram Strand deserves real respect.

I know that wasn't easy. The strength and the cunning of the naga are well known to the night elves. Why? Because we share a history with those scaly bastards.

And it is a history I do not care to repeat. Ever.

original: You are here to offer your services to the Alliance, Adventurer?  We welcome the aid, for although its beauty remains... Ashenvale Forest is not the peaceful place it once was.
text: You're here to offer your services to the Alliance, Adventurer? Good. We'll take the help. Because Ashenvale Forest is still beautiful, sure... but it is a long damn way from the peaceful place it used to be.

original:
Thank you, Adventurer.  It saddens me to order the slaughter of creatures who may not willingly aid our enemies, yet it is my duty to do so.

Your heart might weep for the pridewings you slew, my friend, but may your heart then swell in knowing that your allies are safe from the pridewings' venom.
text:
Thank you, Adventurer. And understand me, it hurts my heart to order the slaughter of creatures that may not even be helping our enemies on purpose. But it's my duty. And duty don't care how I feel.

Your heart might weep for the pridewings you put down, my friend. Let it. Then let it swell, because your allies are safe from that damned venom.

original: We cannot allow the naga to invade our coasts, Adventurer.  It is vital that you go to the Zoram Strand and complete your mission.
text: We cannot let the naga invade our coasts, Adventurer. Not happening. Get your ass to the Zoram Strand and finish your mission.

original: Do you have the pridewing venom sacs, Adventurer?  We cannot allow the orcs to use the beasts' poisons against us!
text: You got those pridewing venom sacs, Adventurer? Because we are not letting those orcs use the beasts' poison against us. Not today, not ever!

original: We elves have a long history.  Let us hope this history does not return to haunt us.
text: We elves have a long, long history. Let's pray to hell that history doesn't come back to haunt us.

original:
If you want to be useful, then why don't you do something about the situation near Talondeep Path?

The transports between Ashenvale and Stonetalon are at a standstill because of the lake coming alive and attacking anything that gets close... which means anyone on the path.  What'd be even more useful than just putting the hammer down on the water elementals there is someone scouting the gazebo on Mystral Lake - the one that has a solid view of the Alliance outpost there.

You up for being useful?
text:
You want to be useful? Then why don't you do something about the mess near Talondeep Path?

The transports between Ashenvale and Stonetalon are dead stopped, because the goddamn lake came alive and attacks anything that gets close. Which means anybody on the path. Water. Attacking people. Unbelievable.

Putting the hammer down on those water elementals would be nice. But you know what'd be even more useful? Somebody scouting the gazebo on Mystral Lake. The one with a solid view of the Alliance outpost there.

So. You up for being useful, or what?

original:
The Earthen Ring is a shamanistic group dedicated to studying and preserving the elements.  They have forgotten more about crazy old gods, ancient legends and lore than most scholars will ever know.

Lucky for you, I know someone in the Earthen Ring here in Ashenvale.  Head over to Zoram'gar Outpost on the coast of the Zoram Strand; show Je'neu Sancrea what you found.  If anyone can figure out that globe's significance, it'd be him.
text:
The Earthen Ring. Shamans who study and protect the elements. Those folks have forgotten more about crazy-ass old gods, ancient legends and lore than most scholars will ever know.

Lucky for you, I know somebody in the Earthen Ring right here in Ashenvale. Head over to Zoram'gar Outpost on the coast of the Zoram Strand and show Je'neu Sancrea what you found. If anybody can figure out what the hell that globe means, it's him.

original:
Yeah, I heard that someone tore up the lake out there like a dust devil through the Barrens.  From the sound of it too, we might be able to set up a possible observation area out there to keep an eye on our Alliance friends.  Well, that is if we can keep it on the down low...

Looks like you ended up being quite useful after all; the transports between here and Stonetalon should have an easier time of it.  Take this - you've earned it.
text:
Yeah, I heard. Somebody tore up that lake like a dust devil ripping through the Barrens. And from the sound of it, we might be able to set up an observation spot out there, keep an eye on our dear Alliance friends. If we can keep it on the down low, that is. Quiet. You understand quiet?

Looks like you turned out to be pretty damn useful after all. The transports between here and Stonetalon should have an easier time now. Take this. You earned it.

original:
You find a nasty ball of water and decide to bring it to me?  Who am I, the Earthen Ring or something?

Actually, that does give me an idea... perhaps you do need the Earthen Ring for this.  I mean, if it helps clear up the situation at the lake for good, then I'm all for it.

You know who the Earthen Ring are, Adventurer?
text:
You find a nasty-ass ball of water, and you decide to bring it to me? Who the hell do I look like, the Earthen Ring?

Actually... hold on. That gives me an idea. Maybe you do need the Earthen Ring for this. If it clears up the shit at that lake for good, I'm all for it.

You know who the Earthen Ring are, Adventurer?

original: You back already?  What's the situation out there - all cleared up now, thanks to you?
text: Back already? So what's the situation out there? All cleaned up now, thanks to you? Yeah?

original: Yeah, what do you need?
text: Yeah? What the hell do you need?

original:
If you want to know about the comings and goings of caravans and merchants here in Splintertree Post, then I am fortunately the orc you are looking for.  Unfortunately for you though, I don't like people.

If you want something, make it quick.
text:
You want to know about the caravans and merchants coming and going here in Splintertree Post? Then lucky you, I'm the orc you're looking for. Unlucky you, I don't like people. At all.

You want something? Make it quick.

original:
You've certainly begun to prove yourself to us, Adventurer. As a reward, please take this care package! Inside it you'll find rations and bandages that are usable only inside Warsong Gulch. 

As you continue to prove yourself inside the Gulch, you'll find that these items will become available to you for purchase. Rations become available when you are Friendly with us, and bandages when you are Honored.
text:
Well, damn. You're starting to prove yourself to us, Adventurer. Here, take this care package! Inside you'll find rations and bandages, and they only work inside Warsong Gulch. Nowhere else, so don't even try.

Keep proving yourself in the Gulch, and you'll be able to buy these yourself. Rations open up when you're Friendly with us, and bandages when you're Honored.

original:
You've certainly begun to prove yourself to us, Adventurer. As a reward, please take this care package! Inside it you'll find rations and bandages that are usable only inside Warsong Gulch. 

As you continue to prove yourself inside the Gulch, you'll find that these items will become available to you for purchase. Rations become available when you are Friendly with us, and bandages when you are Honored.
text:
Look at you, earning your keep with us, Adventurer. That deserves a reward, so here's a care package! Rations and bandages inside. And listen up, they're only usable inside Warsong Gulch.

The more you prove yourself in that Gulch, the more you can just buy this stuff outright. Rations unlock at Friendly with us. Bandages at Honored. Got it?

original:
You've certainly begun to prove yourself to us, Adventurer.  As a reward, please take this care package!  Inside it you'll find rations and bandages that are usable only inside Warsong Gulch.

As you continue to prove yourself inside the Gulch, you'll find that these items will become available to you for purchase.  Rations become available when you are Friendly with us, and bandages when you are Honored.
text:
You are proving yourself to us, Adventurer, no question about it. Take this care package, you earned the hell out of it! It's packed with rations and bandages that only work inside Warsong Gulch.

Keep showing out in the Gulch and these items become yours to buy. Rations when you're Friendly with us. Bandages when you're Honored. Now go make those Horde bastards regret showing up.

original: May the blessings of the night be yours, friend!  I am Illiyana Moonblaze, and I am the main supplier for the Silverwing Sentinels here in Ashenvale.  As you improve your standing with the Sentinels, I will make available to you a fine selection of goods that you can use inside Warsong Gulch.  Should you find yourself in need of item repair, I also provide those services.
text:
May the blessings of the night be yours, friend! I'm Illiyana Moonblaze, main supplier for the Silverwing Sentinels here in Ashenvale.

The better your standing with the Sentinels, the better the goods I'll put in front of you, fine gear you can use inside Warsong Gulch. And if your shit's busted up and needs repair, I handle that too.

original: Thank you, Adventurer. Your exploits in Warsong Gulch ring throughout Ashenvale Forest.
text: Thank you, Adventurer. Your exploits in Warsong Gulch are ringing through every damn tree in Ashenvale Forest.

original: Thank you, Adventurer. Your exploits in Warsong Gulch ring throughout Ashenvale Forest.
text: Thank you, Adventurer. The whole of Ashenvale Forest is talking about what you did in Warsong Gulch. Loud.

original: Thank you, Adventurer. Your exploits in Warsong Gulch ring throughout Ashenvale Forest.
text: Thank you, Adventurer. Word of your hell-raising in Warsong Gulch rings all the way across Ashenvale Forest.

original: Well, you did not flee in the face of defeat. You stood your ground, Adventurer, and when it comes right down to it, that is what makes for a true hero. No doubt you will win next time... but nonetheless we thank you for your effort.
text: Well. You didn't run when defeat came knocking. You stood your ground, Adventurer. And when it comes right down to it, that is what makes a true goddamn hero. You'll win next time, no doubt. But either way, we thank you for your effort.

original: Well, you did not flee in the face of defeat. You stood your ground, Adventurer, and when it comes right down to it, that is what makes for a true hero. No doubt you will win next time... but nonetheless we thank you for your effort.
text: You lost. So what? You didn't flee, Adventurer. You planted your feet and held your ground, and when you strip it all down, that's what a real hero is made of. No doubt you'll take it next time. Still, we thank you for the effort. Damn proud of it, too.

original: You have proven your value to our efforts in Warsong Gulch. Continue to aid the cause and bring me more Marks of Honor. Do this, and you will earn even more of our trust.
text: You have proven your worth to our fight in Warsong Gulch, no doubt about it. Now keep it coming. Keep helping the cause and bring me more Marks of Honor. Do that, and you'll earn even more of our trust. Simple as hell.

original: Thank you, Adventurer. Your exploits in Warsong Gulch ring throughout Ashenvale Forest.
text: Thank you, Adventurer. What you pulled off in Warsong Gulch is echoing through all of Ashenvale Forest. Every last branch of it.

original: Have you fought in Warsong Gulch and defended Silverwing Hold?
text: Well? Have you fought in Warsong Gulch and defended Silverwing Hold, or not?

original: Have you fought in Warsong Gulch and defended Silverwing Hold?
text: Talk to me. You been in Warsong Gulch? You defend Silverwing Hold like I asked?

original: Have you fought in Warsong Gulch and defended Silverwing Hold?
text: So have you done it? Fought in Warsong Gulch? Held the damn line at Silverwing Hold?

original:
My kinfolk were traveling here with many sacred troll charms, but the Thistlefur furbolgs attacked and killed them before they reached Zoram'gar!  Those vile Furbolgs!

I miss my brothers and sisters who were killed, but we will meet again in the afterlife.  However, their troll charms hold great value in this world.  It is an outrage that the furbolgs have them!

Adventurer, you must retrieve the charms!  They are in chests in Thistlefur Hold, a cave at the end of Thistlefur Village, north of Astranaar.
text:
My kinfolk were on their way here carrying a whole lot of sacred troll charms. And the Thistlefur furbolgs jumped them and killed them before they ever reached Zoram'gar! Those vile, flea-bitten, motherfuckin' furbolgs!
