I miss my brothers and sisters. We will meet again in the afterlife, that I know. But those troll charms carry great value in this world. And those bear-faced bastards have them? That is an outrage!

Adventurer, you get those charms back! They're in chests in Thistlefur Hold, a cave at the end of Thistlefur Village, north of Astranaar. Go!

original:
You found them!  Thank you!  Thank you, Adventurer!  You do not know how great a thing you have done for me.

A troll without his charm is like an orc without his battle scars...

Worthless.
text:
You found them! Thank you! Thank you, Adventurer! You have no idea, no damn idea, how great a thing you did for me.

You know what a troll without his charm is? He's like an orc without his battle scars...

Worthless. Goddamn worthless.

original:
You found them!  Thank you!  Thank you, Adventurer!  You do not know how great a thing you have done for me.

A troll without her charm is like an orc without her battle scars...

Worthless.
text:
You found them! Thank you! Thank you, Adventurer! You have no idea, no damn idea, how great a thing you did for me.

You know what a troll without her charm is? She's like an orc without her battle scars...

Worthless. Goddamn worthless.

original: Did you find the charms, Adventurer?  Every moment the furbolgs possess those sacred items, my blood boils with rage!
text: You find the charms, Adventurer? Because every second those furbolgs hold on to my sacred things, my blood is boiling, mon. Boiling!

original: The furbolg were not always our enemy, Adventurer. But times change, and it is no longer a time of peace here in these dark woods.
text: The furbolg weren't always our enemy, Adventurer. But times change. And these dark woods? It sure as hell isn't a time of peace in them anymore.

original: The Sentinels do what they can here in Ashenvale, but it's thanks to travelers like you that we have gained the ground we have.
text: The Sentinels do what they can here in Ashenvale. But the ground we've taken back? We owe a hell of a lot of it to travelers like you.

original: The furbolgs' corruption has caused Ashenvale to become a fraction of its former glory.
text: The furbolgs' damned corruption has left Ashenvale a fraction of the glory it used to be. A fraction!

original: I know these forests as if they were a part of me... but know that there is still much to be learned from them, and much danger still hidden.
text: I know these forests like they're part of my own body... but hear me. There's still a hell of a lot to learn from them. And a hell of a lot of danger still hiding in them.

original: You have completed Teronis' mission, and I appreciate all you have done, adventurer.
text: You finished Teronis' mission. And I appreciate every damn thing you've done, adventurer.

original:
Yes, I expected that you would be back. I sent Korra out earlier and she came across Dartol's Rod, abandoned in the forest.

We worked so hard to recover it, adventurer. Please take care to see that you do not handle it so carelessly in the future.
text:
Yeah. I figured you'd be back. I sent Korra out earlier, and guess what she found? Dartol's Rod. Lying in the forest. Abandoned.

We busted our asses to get that thing back, adventurer. So please, for the love of everything, stop handling it so damn carelessly.

original: You look a bit shaken up, adventurer. Are you well?
text: You look a little shook up, adventurer. You all right? Talk to me.

original: The Sentinels have a great need for supplies to reinforce themselves in Darkshore.
text: The Sentinels in Darkshore need supplies, and they need them bad, to dig in and hold their ground.

original: I heard whisper once that the satyrs' history is somehow related to that of the night elves, but I have found my esteemed hosts reticent to speak of the matter.
text: I heard a whisper once that the satyrs' history is tangled up with the night elves' somehow. But my esteemed hosts? They clam up tight as hell whenever I bring it up.

original: Good day, lad! Perhaps you could help me with some things that need to be taken care of.
text: Good day, lad! Maybe you can help me deal with some shit that needs taking care of.

original: Good day, lass! Perhaps you could help me with some things that need to be taken care of.
text: Good day, lass! Maybe you can help me deal with some shit that needs taking care of.

original: A simple enough task to break this soulstone!
text: Breaking this soulstone? Easy. Simple enough damn task!

original: Then we must put an end to Athrikus Narassin. Tell me, spirit, where might we find the other soulgems, to undo his magic?
text: Then we end Athrikus Narassin. Period. Tell me, spirit, where do we find the other soulgems, so we can tear his goddamn magic apart?

original:
There is evil lurking here along the coast, traveler.

It is the resting place of the doomed city of Zoram, long destroyed and submerged beneath the seas.  Lost, and nearly forgotten.

Now, the naga have returned, and for what reason we do not know.  But reason matters little; we must defend the land we have worked so hard to claim as our own.

Return to me with 20 of their heads! Throw the naga back to the depths!
text:
There is evil creeping along this coast, traveler.

This is the resting place of the doomed city of Zoram. Destroyed long ago and sunk beneath the seas. Lost, and damn near forgotten.

Now the naga are back, and why, we don't know. You know what? Doesn't matter. We fought like hell to claim this land as our own, and we will defend it.

Bring me twenty of their heads! Twenty! Throw those slimy sons of bitches back into the depths!

original: We could use more of your kind around here, Adventurer. Thank you for your help.
text: We could use a lot more of your kind around here, Adventurer. Thank you for the help. Damn good work.

original: The naga increase in numbers, adventurer. Please complete this task for me.
text: The naga keep multiplying, adventurer. More every damn day. Finish this job for me.

original:
As you rummage through Teronis' belongings, you find a journal that is still in good condition.

You take the journal and leave Teronis' corpse as is.

The only thing left to do is find the gem Teronis was seeking. Raene mentioned it being in the area. Perhaps the murlocs have it...
text:
You dig through Teronis' belongings and find a journal, still in good shape.

You take the journal and leave the poor bastard's corpse where it lies.

Only thing left now is to find the gem Teronis was hunting for. Raene said it was somewhere around here. Maybe those murlocs have it... and if they do, God help them.

original:
Teronis' body lies broken atop the island. For some unknown reason, the murlocs have left it alone.

The deep slashes across his corpse obviously came from the weapons and claws of the murlocs.
text:
Teronis' body lies broken on top of the island. And for some damn reason, the murlocs have left it alone.

Those deep slashes all over his corpse? That's murloc work. Their weapons, their claws. Those slimy little bastards.

original: I cannot train a adventurer such as yourself.
text: I can't train an adventurer like you. Not a chance in hell.

original: Through rigorous retraining I have had to break many students of all they had previously learned so that I might teach them anew.  The service I offer becomes increasingly difficult to perform each time it is done.  It is for that reason that it becomes increasingly expensive with each retraining.  Do you desire that I break you of the talents you have learned?
text:
Retraining. Rigorous, painful retraining. I have had to break a lot of students of everything they ever learned, just so I could teach them all over again.

And every time I do it, it gets harder. Harder as hell. That's why it gets more expensive each time. That's not greed, that's the price of pain.

So. You want me to break you of the talents you've learned?

original: Let Kadrak know of the success we have had here holding off the night elves. Our plans are going well.
text: Go tell Kadrak about the success we've had out here holding off those night elves. Our plans are going damn well.

original:
Keep an eye out, traveler. The elves are often hiding in the shadows...

We must always be watching. We have worked very hard to claim this land, and the elves are looking for a chance to take it from us.

I assume you have my next orders from Kadrak?
text:
Keep your eyes open, traveler. Those elves love hiding in the shadows...

We watch. Always. We worked our asses off to claim this land, and those tree-hugging bastards are just waiting for a chance to snatch it back.

I'm guessing you've got my next orders from Kadrak?

original: Your skill exceeds mine, though  I've heard that Old Man Heming in Booty Bay has copies of "The Bass and You".  That is sure to help you increase your skill.
text: Your skill is beyond mine now, mon. But I heard Old Man Heming in Booty Bay has copies of The Bass and You. That book'll push your skill up, no doubt about it.

original: You will need to find Nat Pagle in Dustwallow Marsh to get any better than you are currently.
text: You want to get any better than you are right now? Then you gotta go find Nat Pagle in Dustwallow Marsh. That's it. That's the only damn way.

original: I can teach you fishing skills.
text: I can teach you fishing, mon. Sit your ass down.

original:
Oh, I am so happy Kerlonian made it! And I'm sure I'll find him sleeping somewhere around here, won't I?

Thank you for showing him the way, Adventurer.
text:
Oh, I am so damn happy Kerlonian made it! And I bet I'll find his lazy ass sleeping somewhere around here, won't I?

Thank you for showing him the way, Adventurer.

original: Has Kerlonian arrived?
text: Has Kerlonian shown up yet? Well?

original: You've come for training in order to pass it on to your pets?
text: So you came for training, so you can pass it on to your pets? Good. Let's do this.

original: Ah friend, I only help hunters and their pets.
text: Ah, friend. I only help hunters and their pets. That's it. Nobody else.

original:
Within the beginning tunnels of Blackfathom Deeps, large sapphire clusters can be found along the cave walls. Recently it was noted that the naga were harvesting the crystals. Until it can be discerned why, I sense we should stop the naga from succeeding. The crystals have great elemental power and if used inappropriately, could make for a powerful arcane component.

Will you help me, Adventurer? Blackfathom Deeps can be found along Zoram Strand to the north of our outpost.
text:
Listen up, Adventurer. In the beginnin' tunnels of Blackfathom Deeps, there's big sapphire clusters growin' right outta the cave walls. And guess who's been seen harvestin' them crystals? The goddamn naga. Now, I don't know why yet. But until I do, I sense we need to stop those slippery motherfuckers from succeedin'.

Them crystals carry serious elemental power. In the wrong hands, they make one hell of an arcane component. You hear me? One hell of a component.

So, will you help me? Blackfathom Deeps sits along Zoram Strand, to the north of our outpost. Go get me those crystals.

original:
This Twilight's Hammer follower cannot be allowed to complete his plan. The Twilight's Hammer do not understand the spirits of nature. They believe in the Old Gods--creatures of chaos and destruction that were long ago defeated. This Lorgus cannot be allowed to succeed. You must stop him, Adventurer. I cannot do it myself--I am too weak.

Go into Blackfathom Deeps, find him, and kill him. Return to me here at Zoram'gar when it's done.
text:
This Twilight's Hammer follower cannot, will not, be allowed to finish his plan. Them fools don't understand the spirits of nature. Not one damn bit. They worship the Old Gods, creatures of chaos and destruction that got their asses beat a long, long time ago. And this Lorgus wants to bring that shit back?

No. You must stop him, Adventurer. I'd do it myself, but I'm too damn weak right now.

So go into Blackfathom Deeps. Find him. Kill him. Then come back to me here at Zoram'gar when the son of a bitch is done.

original:
The Twilight's Hammer has moved into the Moonshrine Ruins of Blackfathom Deeps.  Their presence can only serve to coerce the elements into working against us.  If left unchecked, this region will be theirs for good.

Adventurer, go into Blackfathom and find the ruin's fathom stone; it should be somewhere close in the water.  In it is a fathom core - a device that when properly read it will relate a history of all elemental activity.  If I have it, I and the Earthen Ring can maybe do something to stop them!
text:
The Twilight's Hammer done moved into the Moonshrine Ruins of Blackfathom Deeps. You know what their presence does? It twists the elements, bends 'em into workin' against us. Leave 'em be, and this whole region is theirs for good. For good, mon!

Adventurer, get into Blackfathom and find the ruin's fathom stone. It should be somewhere close, in the water. Inside it is a fathom core, a device that, read properly, tells the history of every damn bit of elemental activity. You bring me that, and me and the Earthen Ring can maybe shut these cultist motherfuckers down.

original:
This globe... it is most disturbing.  Many of the more powerful elementals receive their power and energy through such devices.  To find one like this nearly intact is one thing - to find it so tainted is another.

I will see that this globe is studied properly by the Earthen Ring.  Perhaps we can bring an end to this corruption of the elements.  Please - accept this as a fair exchange for bringing this globe to the attention of the Earthen Ring.
text:
This globe... this globe is disturbin', friend. Deeply disturbin'. A lot of the more powerful elementals draw their power and energy through devices just like this. Findin' one nearly intact? That's one thing. Findin' it tainted like this? That's some other shit entirely.

I will see this globe studied properly by the Earthen Ring. Maybe we can put an end to this corruption of the elements, once and for all. Please, take this. A fair exchange for bringin' this globe to the Earthen Ring's attention.

original:
This... this is quite the find, Adventurer.

You acquired this from Baron Aquanis in Blackfathom, you say? Baron Aquanis has long been thought of as a corrupted elemental power; this globe will prove what exactly had corrupted him. While it would be no surprise if it turned out to be the Twilight's Hammer, our studies will also show how they did it as well.

You did well in bringing this to me. Please - take this, along with the Earthen Ring's warmest regards.
text:
Well, damn. This... this is quite the find, Adventurer.

You took this off Baron Aquanis, in Blackfathom? Baron Aquanis been thought of as a corrupted elemental power for a long time. This globe gonna prove exactly what corrupted him. If it turns out to be the Twilight's Hammer, I won't be surprised one bit. But our studies will show how they did it, too. Every last filthy detail.

You did good bringin' this to me. Please, take this, along with the Earthen Ring's warmest regards.

original: Tsunaman sent you? Excellent. Then we have matters to discuss.
text: Tsunaman sent you? Good. Excellent. Then sit your ass down, because we got matters to discuss.

original:
Well done, Adventurer. These are the crystals I spoke of. Intriguing...

I can feel the power within them. The spirits of water cling to them. Whatever the naga were going to use these for... well, let us be glad they are no longer in their hands.
text:
Well done, Adventurer. These the crystals I was talkin' about. Interestin'...

I can feel the power inside 'em. The spirits of water cling to these things like their lives depend on it. Whatever them naga were plannin' to do with 'em... well, let's just be damn glad they ain't in their hands no more.

original:
This is interesting indeed. I am glad you have brought it to my attention.

Now we have a name for our troubles... Lorgus Jett.
text:
Now this... this is interestin' indeed. I'm glad you brought this to me.

'Cause now our troubles got a name. Lorgus Jett. Remember it, friend. Lorgus. Motherfuckin'. Jett.

original:
Very good!! Thank you, Adventurer. We may not have stopped the Twilight's Hammer completely, but at least you have staved off another of their plans to return the Old Gods to power.

Who knows what other plans they have manifesting, but we can rest easy for now.
text:
Very good! Very damn good! Thank you, Adventurer. We may not have stopped the Twilight's Hammer completely, but you staved off one more of their sick plans to put the Old Gods back in power.

Who knows what other shit they got cookin'. But for now? For now, we can rest easy.

original:
This is exactly what I need!  A fathom core is an incredible well of information that we will be able to draw much good from.  Whatever the Twilight's Hammer is up to in there - and believe me when I say it is no good - my comrades and I will now uncover.

You've done well here today; the Earthen Ring looks upon you warmly for assisting us.  You've also helped the Horde as a whole, and for that you should be proud.
text:
This is exactly what I need! Exactly! A fathom core is an incredible well of information, and we gonna draw a whole lot of good out of it. Whatever the Twilight's Hammer is up to down there, and believe me, it ain't no damn good, me and my comrades are gonna dig it all up.

You did well today. The Earthen Ring looks on you warmly for helpin' us. And you helped the whole Horde, too. Be proud of that, friend. You earned it.

original:
This... this is quite the find, Adventurer.

You acquired this from Baron Aquanis in Blackfathom, you say?  Baron Aquanis has long been thought of as a corrupted elemental power; this globe will prove what exactly had corrupted him.  While it would be no surprise if it turned out to be the Twilight's Hammer, our studies will also show how they did it as well.

You did well in bringing this to me.  Please - take this, along with the Earthen Ring's warmest regards.
text:
Hold on now. This... this is a hell of a find, Adventurer.

You got this from Baron Aquanis, down in Blackfathom? Baron Aquanis been considered a corrupted elemental power for ages. This globe will prove exactly what corrupted him. If it was the Twilight's Hammer, I ain't gonna be shocked. But our studies will show how those bastards pulled it off, too.

You did right bringin' this to me. Please, take this, with the Earthen Ring's warmest regards.

original:
Ah, hello there.  I spend a great deal of time studying the water - all the elements really - so much so that sometimes I don't even notice people around me.

Is there something I can help you with?
text:
Ah. Hello there. Sorry, I spend so damn much time studyin' the water, all the elements really, that sometimes I don't even notice folks standin' right in front of me.

So. Is there somethin' I can help you with?

original: Uldaman is an ancient Titan vault that has laid buried within the earth since the world's creation. Dwarven excavations of the city have recently released the Titans' first failed creations: the troggs. Legends say that when the Titans deemed the trogg experiment a failure they tried again, resulting in the creation of the dwarven race. These secrets are recorded on the fabled Discs of Norgannon - massive artifacts that lie at the bottom of the ancient city, protected by giant constructs of living stone.
text:
Uldaman. An ancient Titan vault, buried in the earth since the world was made. And what did the dwarves do? They dug it up, and let loose the Titans' first failed creations. The troggs. Ugly, stupid, motherfuckin' troggs.

Legends say that when the Titans called the trogg experiment a failure, they tried again, and that's how the dwarven race came to be. Those secrets are written on the fabled Discs of Norgannon, massive artifacts at the bottom of the ancient city. And guardin' them? Giant constructs of living stone. Good luck with that shit.

original: This sun-blasted city is home to the Sandfury trolls, known for their particular ruthlessness and dark mysticism. Troll legends tell of a powerful sword called Sul'thraze the Lasher, a weapon capable of instilling fear and weakness in even the most formidable of foes. Long ago, the weapon was split in half. However, rumors have circulated that the two halves may be found somewhere within Zul'Farrak's walls.
text:
Zul'Farrak. A sun-blasted hellhole of a city, home to the Sandfury trolls. Ruthless sons of bitches, and deep into dark mysticism.

Troll legends talk about a sword called Sul'thraze the Lasher. A weapon that puts fear and weakness into even the toughest bastard alive. Long ago, somebody split that blade in half. But the rumor goes, both halves might be sittin' somewhere inside Zul'Farrak's walls. Waitin' on somebody crazy enough to go get 'em.

original: Once the capital city of the Dark Iron dwarves, this volcanic labyrinth now serves as the seat of power for Ragnaros the Firelord. Ragnaros has uncovered the secret to creating life from stone and plans to build an army of unstoppable golems to aid him in conquering the whole of Blackrock Mountain. Obsessed with defeating Nefarian and his draconic minions, Ragnaros will go to any extreme to achieve final victory.
text:
This volcanic labyrinth used to be the capital of the Dark Iron dwarves. Now? Now it's the seat of power for Ragnaros the Firelord himself.

Ragnaros figured out the secret to makin' life from stone, and he's buildin' an army of unstoppable golems to help him take the whole of Blackrock Mountain. He's obsessed with beatin' Nefarian and his draconic minions. Obsessed. That fiery son of a bitch will go to any extreme to win.

original: Over a thousand years ago a group of troll priests known as the Atal'ai attempted to bring back an ancient blood god named Hakkar the Soulflayer. After the resulting civil war the priests were defeated and exiled to the Swamp of Sorrows. There they erected a temple to Hakkar to prepare for his arrival into the physical world. The dragon Aspect Ysera soon learned of the Atal'ai's plans and smashed the temple beneath the marshes. To this day, the temple's ruins are guarded by the mighty green dragons.
text:
Over a thousand years ago, a bunch of troll priests called the Atal'ai tried to bring back an ancient blood god. Hakkar the Soulflayer. Now who in their right damn mind does that?

After the civil war that followed, the priests got beaten and exiled to the Swamp of Sorrows. And what did they do there? Built a temple to Hakkar, to get ready for his arrival into the physical world. Then the dragon Aspect Ysera found out about the Atal'ai's plans, and she smashed that temple right down beneath the marshes. To this day, the ruins are guarded by the mighty green dragons. Think about that before you go stompin' in there.

original: The mighty fortress carved within the fiery bowels of Blackrock Mountain was held by the sinister Dark Iron dwarves for centuries until Nefarian - the cunning son of the dragon, Deathwing - took control of the upper Spire and made war on the dwarves' holdings in the mountain's volcanic depths. Realizing that the dwarves were led by the mighty fire elemental, Ragnaros - Nefarian vowed to crush his enemies and claim the whole of Blackrock mountain for himself.
text:
That mighty fortress, carved into the fiery bowels of Blackrock Mountain? The sinister Dark Iron dwarves held it for centuries. Centuries! Until Nefarian, the cunning son of the dragon Deathwing, took the upper Spire and went to war on the dwarves' holdings down in the volcanic depths.

Then he figured out who was really pullin' the dwarves' strings. Ragnaros, the mighty fire elemental. And Nefarian swore he'd crush his enemies and take the whole of Blackrock mountain for himself. Dragons and fire lords, friend. That whole mountain is one big goddamn war.

original: Built twelve thousand years ago by a covert sect of night elf sorcerers, the ancient city of Eldre'Thalas was used to protect Queen Azshara's most prized arcane secrets. Though it was ravaged by the Great Sundering of the world, much of the wondrous city still stands as the imposing Dire Maul. The ruins' three distinct districts have been overrun by all manner of creatures - especially the spectral highborne, foul satyr and brutish ogres.
text:
Twelve thousand years ago, a secret sect of night elf sorcerers built the ancient city of Eldre'Thalas, to guard Queen Azshara's most prized arcane secrets.

The Great Sundering tore the world apart, but a whole lot of that wondrous city is still standin'. We call it Dire Maul now. Its three districts are crawlin' with every kind of creature you can name. Spectral highborne. Foul-ass satyr. Big, dumb, brutish ogres. Watch yourself in there.

original: Once the jewel of northern Lordaeron, the city of Stratholme is where Prince Arthas turned against his mentor, Uther Lightbringer, and slaughtered hundreds of his own subjects who were believed to have contracted the plague of undeath. Arthas' surrender to the Lich King soon followed. The broken city is now inhabited by the undead Scourge - led by the powerful lich, Kel'Thuzad, and a contingent of Scarlet Crusaders, led by Grand Crusader Dathrohan. The two sides are locked in constant, violent combat.
text:
Stratholme. Once the jewel of northern Lordaeron. It's where Prince Arthas turned on his own mentor, Uther Lightbringer, and slaughtered hundreds of his own people, 'cause he believed they'd caught the plague of undeath. Not long after, Arthas gave himself up to the Lich King.

Now that broken city belongs to the undead Scourge, led by the powerful lich, Kel'Thuzad. And fightin' them, every damn day, is a contingent of Scarlet Crusaders, led by Grand Crusader Dathrohan. The two sides are locked in constant, bloody, violent combat. Nobody's winnin'. Everybody's dyin'.

original: The Scholomance is housed in crypts beneath the Caer Darrow keep. Once owned by the noble Barov family, the keep fell to ruin after the Second War. As the wizard Kel'Thuzad enlisted followers for his Cult of the Damned, he often promised immortality for those who served his Lich King. The Barovs fell to his influence and donated their keep, but the cultists killed the family and turned the crypts into a school of necromancy. Though Kel'Thuzad no longer resides there, cultists and instructors still remain.
text:
The Scholomance sits in the crypts under the Caer Darrow keep. That keep used to belong to the noble Barov family, but it went to ruin after the Second War.

Then along came the wizard Kel'Thuzad, recruitin' for his Cult of the Damned, promisin' immortality to anybody who'd serve his Lich King. The Barovs bought that bullshit and gave up their keep. And what did they get for it? The cultists murdered the whole family and turned the crypts into a school of necromancy. Kel'Thuzad ain't there no more, but his cultists and instructors sure as hell are.

original:
I understand that it can be difficult at times to come out on top in Warsong Gulch. Still, your effort on our behalf - even when victory is not achieved - is important.

Should you complete one of the trials inside Warsong Gulch and not achieve victory, you will still receive a Ribbons of Sacrifice. Bring it to me so that the Sentinels may reward you for acting on our behalf... even if you weren't able to win this time.
text:
Look, I get it. Sometimes you just can't come out on top in Warsong Gulch. Shit happens. But your effort for us, even when you lose, still matters. You hear me? It matters.

If you finish one of the trials in Warsong Gulch and don't win, you still get a Ribbons of Sacrifice. Bring it to me, and the Sentinels will reward you for fightin' on our behalf. Even if you got your ass handed to you this time.

original:
Beyond this tunnel you will find a field of strife and turmoil, young adventurer. The Horde continue to decimate our sacred forest, cutting down the evergreen foliage to power their machines of war.

Enter Warsong Gulch and defend Silverwing Hold. Push back the invading Horde forces!

Do this, and earn a Mark of Honor.  Bring it to me, Adventurer, and I shall reward you.
text:
Past this tunnel, young adventurer, is a field of strife and turmoil. The Horde keep tearin' through our sacred forest, choppin' down the evergreen foliage to feed their goddamn war machines.

Get into Warsong Gulch and defend Silverwing Hold. Push those invading Horde forces back where they came from!

Do that, and you'll earn a Mark of Honor. Bring it to me, Adventurer, and I'll make it worth your while.

original: You have proven your value to our efforts in Warsong Gulch. Continue to aid the cause and bring me more Marks of Honor. Do this, and you will earn even more of our trust.
text: You've proven your worth to our fight in Warsong Gulch, no doubt about it. Now keep it up. Bring me more Marks of Honor. Do that, and you'll earn even more of our trust.

original: You have proven your value to our efforts in Warsong Gulch. Continue to aid the cause and bring me more Marks of Honor. Do this, and you will earn even more of our trust.
text: Damn right, you've shown your value in Warsong Gulch. But we ain't done. Keep aiding the cause and bring me more Marks of Honor. You do that, and our trust in you only grows.

original: You have proven your value to our efforts in Warsong Gulch. Continue to aid the cause and bring me more Marks of Honor. Do this, and you will earn even more of our trust.
text: Look at you. Proving yourself out there in Warsong Gulch, over and over. Don't stop now. Bring me more Marks of Honor, and you'll earn even more of our trust.

original: You have proven your value to our efforts in Warsong Gulch. Continue to aid the cause and bring me more Marks of Honor. Do this, and you will earn even more of our trust.
text: Again? Hell yes. You keep showing your value in Warsong Gulch. Keep fighting for the cause and keep bringing me more Marks of Honor. Do that, and you earn even more of our trust.

original: Thank you, Adventurer. Your exploits in Warsong Gulch ring throughout Ashenvale Forest.
text: Thank you, Adventurer. Your exploits in Warsong Gulch are ringin' all through Ashenvale Forest. Everybody's talkin' about it.

original:
The Forsaken, the undead arm of the Horde, have crept into Ashenvale, lurking at our ruins and our barrows.  We believe their goal is to spread disease amongst the lands of the night elves.  We must confirm this!

The Forsaken have a camp south of here, near the Dor'Danil Barrow Den, where they create poisons and diseases and place them in bottles.  Fight your way into that camp and steal a bottle of disease.  Return with such a bottle.  I will test it and find its purpose.
text:
The Forsaken. The undead arm of the Horde. They've crept into Ashenvale, lurkin' around our ruins and our barrows like the rotten vermin they are. We believe they mean to spread disease across the lands of the night elves. And we need to confirm it!

Those dead bastards got a camp south of here, near the Dor'Danil Barrow Den, where they brew poisons and diseases and stick 'em in bottles. Fight your way into that camp and steal me a bottle of disease. Bring it back. I'll test it and find out what the hell they're up to.

original:
When I struggled with the Forsaken's poisons, I had a vision.  I had a vision of the druids in the Dor'danil Barrow Den, poisoned... murdered by the undead!  They are now errant ghosts, severed from their bodies and driven mad.

So that the druids' spirits might some day find peace, you must enter the Dor'danil Barrow Den and destroy its once great leaders: Taneel Darkwood, Uthil Mooncall and Mavoris Cloudsbreak.

Do this, then return to me.
text:
When I was fighting the Forsaken's poisons, I had a vision. A vision of the druids in the Dor'danil Barrow Den, poisoned... murdered by those undead sons of bitches! Now they're errant ghosts, cut off from their bodies, and driven out of their goddamn minds.

So their spirits can someday find peace, you have to go into the Dor'danil Barrow Den and destroy their once great leaders. Taneel Darkwood. Uthil Mooncall. Mavoris Cloudsbreak.

Do it. Then come back to me.

original: Very good, Adventurer.  Now... by testing the contents of this bottle, the goals of the Forsaken will be revealed!
text: Very good, Adventurer. Very good. Now... once I test what's in this bottle, the Forsaken's whole damn plan is gonna be laid bare!

original:
I felt the anguish of the Dor'danil Barrows lessen, and knew you had completed your task.

It was grim work you did, Adventurer, for the spirits you destroyed were merely victims of the Forsaken's evil.  But with their destruction, let us hope the other maddened spirits find peace.
text:
I felt the anguish of the Dor'danil Barrows ease up, and I knew. I knew you'd done it.

That was grim work, Adventurer. Those spirits you put down were victims, nothin' but victims of the Forsaken's evil. That's what pisses me off. But with them gone, let's pray the other maddened spirits finally find some peace.

original:
Yes, Adventurer. Felwood has been through much hardship. Thank you for what you have done.

One day, we may be able to reclaim Felwood from the corruption; every kind deed helps.
text:
Yes, Adventurer. Felwood has been through some shit. Some real shit. Thank you for what you've done.

One day, we may take Felwood back from the corruption. And every kind deed, every single one, gets us closer.

original: Ah, Shindrell's report!  Many thanks, Adventurer.  Shindrell is a fine sentinel, brave and keen.  I must read this for clues of a wickedness I fear is moving through Ashenvale.
text: Ah, Shindrell's report! Thank you, Adventurer. Shindrell's a fine sentinel. Brave, sharp as hell. Now let me read this, 'cause I got a bad feelin' some kind of wickedness is movin' through Ashenvale.

original: Did you find the camp, Adventurer?  Do you have a bottle of disease?
text: Well? Did you find the camp, Adventurer? You got me that bottle of disease or not?

original: The anguish of the Dor'danil druids still haunt my dreams, Adventurer. You must destroy their leaders!
text: The anguish of the Dor'danil druids is still haunting my damn dreams, Adventurer. You have to destroy their leaders!

original: What have you seen in this corrupted land?
text: Tell me straight. What have you seen out in that corrupted hellscape?

original: Do you have something for me?
text: You got somethin' for me, or what?

original: The balance of nature is a delicate one, and easily tipped.  Are you brave enough to make things right?
text: The balance of nature is a delicate thing, friend. Easy as hell to tip over. So let me ask you. Are you brave enough to make it right?

original: Uh... the disease is potent.  And it attacks the mind...
text: Ugh... this disease is potent. Goddamn potent. And it's goin' after my mind...

original: I must... RESIST!
text: I must... RESIST! Not today, motherfucker!

original: I have survived the poisons of the Forsaken, adventurer, and I know now what must be done.
text: I survived the Forsaken's poisons, adventurer. Survived 'em. And now I know exactly what has to be done.

original: If we are to make these new lands ours then we must have places to rest our battle weary bodies. Lay your axe by the fire and share the stories of your mighty battles.
text: If we're gonna make these new lands ours, we need somewhere to rest these battle-weary bodies. So lay your axe by the fire, sit your ass down, and tell me about your mighty damn battles.

original: No, I'm not, but lots of others are looking for love.  You should buy my love tokens, put on some cologne or perfume, and then pass them around!
text: No, I'm not. But plenty of other folks are lookin' for love. So buy my love tokens, slap on some cologne or perfume, and pass 'em around!

original: Are you interested in exploring one of these dungeons?
text: So. You lookin' to go explore one of these dungeons?

original:
If you put on cologne or perfume, then you'll see who is amorous.  Those are the ones who accept love tokens... and offer a gift in return.

But remember: to give someone a love token, you have to smell just right!  Men like the scent of perfume, while women prefer cologne.
text:
Put on cologne or perfume, and you'll see who's feelin' amorous. Those are the ones who'll take love tokens... and give you a gift back.

But remember this, and remember it good. To give somebody a love token, you gotta smell just right! Men like the scent of perfume. Women prefer cologne. Don't screw it up.

original:
Love tokens are small messages of affection you can give to amorous town and city folk.  Such people will reward you with a gift of adoration.

Or, if you are already adored by another, then at the least they'll give you a gift of friendship.
text:
Love tokens are little messages of affection you hand out to amorous town and city folk. Give 'em one, and they'll reward you with a gift of adoration.

And if you're already adored by somebody else? Then at the very least, they'll give you a gift of friendship. Not a bad damn deal.

original:
When you give love tokens to townsfolk, you'll receive different gifts in return.  Some of those you'll want to keep and use, but others can be bundled together and given to your favorite hero!  Visit Kwee Q. Peddlefeet to turn them in.

Kwee can be found near Bolvar, Magni, or Tyrande.
text:
Hand love tokens to townsfolk and you'll get all kinds of gifts back. Some you'll wanna keep and use. The rest? Bundle that stuff together and give it to your favorite hero! Go see Kwee Q. Peddlefeet to turn 'em in.

You'll find Kwee near Bolvar, Magni, or Tyrande.

original:
When you give love tokens to townsfolk, you'll receive different gifts in return.  Some of those you'll want to keep and use, but others can be bundled together and given to your favorite hero!  Visit Kwee Q. Peddlefeet to turn them in.

Kwee can be found near Cairne, Sylvanas and Thrall.
text:
Give love tokens to townsfolk, and you'll get different gifts back. Some are worth keepin'. The others, you bundle up and hand to your favorite hero! Take 'em to Kwee Q. Peddlefeet.

Kwee hangs around near Cairne, Sylvanas and Thrall.

original: Ragefire Chasm can be found beneath the Shadow Cleft in the center of Orgrimmar.
text: Ragefire Chasm? It's under the Shadow Cleft, right in the center of Orgrimmar. Under our own damn feet.

original: The Deadmines can be found beneath Moonbrook in the south of Westfall.
text: The Deadmines are down beneath Moonbrook, in the south of Westfall. Go on, get your ass over there.

original: The Wailing Caverns has its entrance at the Lushwater Oasis southwest of Crossroads in the Barrens.
text: Wailing Caverns? The entrance is at the Lushwater Oasis, southwest of Crossroads in the Barrens. Don't get lost, damn it.

original: Shadowfang Keep is in southern Silverpine just north of Pyrewood Village.
text: Shadowfang Keep sits in southern Silverpine, just north of Pyrewood Village. Creepy-ass place.

original: Blackfathom Deeps can be found at the north end of Zoram Strand along the coast of Ashenvale.
text: Blackfathom Deeps is up at the north end of Zoram Strand, on the coast of Ashenvale. Hope you can hold your breath.

original: The Stormwind Stockades are found near the mage quarter in Stormwind.
text: The Stormwind Stockades? Near the mage quarter, in Stormwind. Yeah, right in the middle of the humans' city. Good luck.

original: Razorfen Kraul can be found on the very southern tip of the Barrens on the west side of the road.
text: Razorfen Kraul is at the very southern tip of the Barrens, on the west side of the road. West, not east. Remember that.

original: Gnomeregan can be found in western Dun Morogh.
text: Gnomeregan's in western Dun Morogh. Cold as hell up there.

original: Scarlet Monastery lies in the hills northeast of Tirisfal Glades.
text: Scarlet Monastery's up in the hills, northeast of Tirisfal Glades. Go on, you can't miss it.

original: Razorfen Downs can be found on the very southern tip of the Barrens on the east side of the road.
text: Razorfen Downs is at the very southern tip of the Barrens, on the east side of the road. East side, friend. Don't get lost.

original: Maraudon is located in the middle of the western coast of Desolace, in the Valley of Spears.
text: Maraudon is smack in the middle of the western coast of Desolace, in the Valley of Spears. Ugliest damn stretch of land you ever saw.

original: Uldaman can be found at the very northern end of the Badlands.
text: Uldaman? You'll find it at the very northern end of the Badlands. Bring water.

original: The ruins of Zul'Farrak are located in the northwestern corner of the Tanaris Desert.
text: The ruins of Zul'Farrak are in the northwestern corner of the Tanaris Desert. Hot as hell out there.

original: Blackrock Mountain lies between Searing Gorge in the north and Burning Steppes in the south.
text: Blackrock Mountain sits right between Searing Gorge in the north and Burning Steppes in the south. Big, burnin' son of a bitch. Can't miss it.

original: The Sunken Temple can be found in the center of a great lake in eastern Swamp of Sorrows.
text: The Sunken Temple is in the middle of a great big lake, in eastern Swamp of Sorrows. Hope you like gettin' wet.

original: The ruins of Dire Maul stand in central Ferelas.
text: The ruins of Dire Maul stand in central Ferelas. Big old ruins. You'll see 'em.

original: The ruined city of Stratholme lies in the Eastern Plaguelands to the north of the Plaguewood.
text: Stratholme? That ruined city is in the Eastern Plaguelands, north of the Plaguewood. Hell on earth, friend.

original:
I would charge you with a task, Adventurer.

I was on my small vessel, skimming over the submerged ruins of Zoram, when naga attacked me, surging from the water and tearing at me with their claws!  I fled, carrying what supplies I could to make this meager camp.

But when I reached the shore and ran... my prized possession was lost.

Please, Adventurer, find the site of my ambush, along the coast to the north, and search for an ancient statuette.  It is the reason I have braved the dangers of the Zoram Strand.
text:
Adventurer. I got a job for you.

I was out on my little boat, skimmin' over the submerged ruins of Zoram, when the goddamn naga hit me. Came surgin' up out of the water, tearin' at me with their claws! I ran, grabbed what supplies I could, and threw together this sorry-ass camp.

But somewhere between the shore and here... I lost my prized possession.

Please. Find the spot where they ambushed me, along the coast to the north, and search for an ancient statuette. That statuette is the whole damn reason I braved the Zoram Strand in the first place.

original:
I fear the ancient statuette's secrets will remain forever hidden unless you find the key to its ancient lock.

That key is a ring, the Ring of Zoram.  It belonged to the rulers of this city before the waves of the Sundering drowned it.

For years the ring was lost, but the naga have recently found it.

Their leader, Ruuzel, dwells on an isle on the northern edge of Zoram.  Please, Adventurer, retrieve the ring for me!
text:
I'm afraid this ancient statuette's secrets are gonna stay locked up forever, unless you find the key to its ancient lock.

That key is a ring. The Ring of Zoram. It belonged to the rulers of this city, before the waves of the Sundering drowned the whole damn place.

That ring was lost for years. And now? Now the naga found it. Of course they did.

Their leader, Ruuzel, lives on an isle at the northern edge of Zoram. Please, Adventurer. Go take that ring back from the scaly son of a bitch!

original:
You found it!  Thank you, Adventurer!

The old city of Zoram holds many secrets, and this statuette may be the key to many of them.
text:
You found it! Hot damn, you actually found it! Thank you, Adventurer!

The old city of Zoram holds a whole lot of secrets. And this statuette might be the key to a hell of a lot of them.

original: You found the ring!  Thank you, Adventurer.  Please take this as payment, and know that your deeds today will remain forever in my memory.
text: You got the ring! Thank you, Adventurer. Take this as payment. And know what you did today is stayin' in my memory forever. Forever, friend.

original: Have you found the statuette, Adventurer?
text: Well? You find my statuette yet, Adventurer?

original: It is said that the Ring of Zoram is the key to any lock within the city.  Do you have it, Adventurer?
text: They say the Ring of Zoram opens any lock in the city. Any lock. So tell me, Adventurer. Do you have the damn thing?

original: This statuette must hold a hidden compartment...
text: This statuette's gotta have a hidden compartment in it somewhere...

original: It's locked!  NO!!
text: It's locked! NO! Son of a bitch!

original: adventurer, I am in need of your help once again.
text: Adventurer. Hate to ask again, but I need your damn help one more time.

original:
There is a plant that once grew in the old ruins of Bathran's Haunt to the north.  The plant was called Bathran's Hair and was known to cure ailments of the spirit.

There is a sick child in the village, and I believe it is more than just a physical illness.  Will you go to Bathran's Haunt and search it for Bathran's Hair?  I may need it to properly treat the child.

Bathran's Haunt lies north of Maestra's Post and just south of the border to Darkshore.
text:
There's a plant that used to grow in the old ruins of Bathran's Haunt, up to the north. They called it Bathran's Hair. It was known to cure sickness of the spirit.

Now there's a sick child in this village. And I'm tellin' you, this ain't just some physical illness. So will you go to Bathran's Haunt and search that place for Bathran's Hair? I might need it to treat that kid right.

Bathran's Haunt is north of Maestra's Post, just south of the border to Darkshore. Move your ass.

original:
Adventurer, I have created a cure that I believe will help the afflicted child.  Take it to Astranaar and give it to the child's parent, Pelturas Whitemoon.

To reach Astranaar, follow the road south, then east.
text:
Adventurer, I made a cure. I believe it'll help that sick child. Take it to Astranaar and put it in the hands of the child's parent, Pelturas Whitemoon. Nobody else.

To get to Astranaar, follow the road south, then east. Now go, damn it, that kid's waitin'.

original:
Ah, you have the hair!  Now I will mix a cure for the child, and pray my concoction works.

And... Forsaken are at Bathran's Haunt?  Very troubling to hear, that is.  Very troubling indeed...
text:
Ah, you got the hair! Good. Now I'll mix a cure for that child, and pray to every spirit out there that my concoction works.

And wait... the Forsaken are at Bathran's Haunt? Well, that's troubling as hell to hear. Very troubling indeed...

original: Have you gathered the Bathran's Hair, Adventurer?  The child's health grows weaker by the hour...
text: You got that Bathran's Hair yet, Adventurer? That child is gettin' weaker by the goddamn hour...

original: Ashenvale is a lush forest, brimming with life. It is a pleasure to walk down its secret paths in search of herbs, but one must take care. The forest is not without its dangers.
text: Ashenvale is a lush forest, brimmin' with life. Walkin' its secret paths huntin' for herbs? That's a pleasure, friend. But you watch yourself. This forest got its dangers, and they will fuck you up.

original: The mixture is finished, adventurer.  Now we must save the child.
text: The mixture's done, adventurer. Now we gotta save that damn child.

original:
We are in short supply of a few items at the Warsong lumber camp!

Pixel at Splintertree Post has our shipment of saw blades. It'll take a trip to Booty Bay to pick up a crate of axes from Wharfmaster Lozgil.

Our shipment of oil and rope will be more difficult. The rope was pilfered by the Thistlefur and Foulweald furbolgs, and the satyrs intercepted the delivery of the oil and are now using it for detestable rituals in Night Run, Satyrnaar, and Xavian!

Can you help me?
text:
We are runnin' short on a whole pile of shit at the Warsong lumber camp!

Pixel at Splintertree Post has our shipment of saw blades. Then somebody's gotta make the trip to Booty Bay to grab a crate of axes from Wharfmaster Lozgil.

The oil and rope? That's where it gets ugly. The rope got stolen by the Thistlefur and Foulweald furbolgs. And the satyrs hijacked the oil delivery, and now those horned freaks are usin' it for their detestable rituals in Night Run, Satyrnaar, and Xavian!

So, can you help me or not?

original:
Excellent, Adventurer. You've saved me a lot of work!

But don't think that I'm not grateful!
text:
Excellent, Adventurer. You just saved me a whole lot of damn work!

And don't you dare think I ain't grateful!

original: I hope you can come through with the supplies! I'm in big trouble if I don't deliver them soon!
text: Tell me you're comin' through with those supplies! 'Cause if I don't deliver 'em soon, my ass is in big trouble!

original:
I just picked up this shredder from Ratchet and I was on my way back to the Warsong Lumber Camp, where I am supposed to be on duty. I was given a manual on how to operate the shredder, but on the trip back, a huge gust of wind blew it from my hands. The pages went everywhere, and all I was left with was the cover.

The pages could be just about anywhere by now, I suppose... but I don't know how to use the shredder without them! Will you find them for me?
text:
So I just picked up this shredder from Ratchet, and I was headin' back to the Warsong Lumber Camp, where I'm supposed to be on duty. They gave me a manual on how to run the thing. And then? A huge goddamn gust of wind ripped it right out of my hands. Pages flew everywhere. All I got left is the cover.

Those pages could be just about anywhere by now... but I can't run this shredder without 'em! Will you find them for me?

original: Reading isn't my strong point... but now I'll be able to get back to work! Thanks, Adventurer!
text: Readin' ain't exactly my strong point... but hell, now I can get back to work! Thanks, Adventurer!

original: I hope you find the pages soon, Adventurer! I really need to get back to work!
text: Hurry up and find those pages, Adventurer! I really gotta get back to work before somebody chews my ass out!

original: Ishnu-dal-dieb, adventurer. Have you come here in search of knowledge?
text: Ishnu-dal-dieb, adventurer. So. You came here lookin' for knowledge?

original: Teaching is not a one-sided trade, adventurer. As I teach you, I learn more myself, and my understanding grows.
text: Teachin' ain't a one-sided trade, adventurer. Every damn time I teach you something, I learn more myself, and my understanding grows.

original: My apologies, adventurer, but I do not offer instruction to novices. Instead, talk to Milla Fairancora in the Craftsmen's Terrace of Darnassus. She can help you make up for lost time.
text: Sorry, adventurer, but I don't teach novices. Not my job. Go talk to Milla Fairancora, in the Craftsmen's Terrace of Darnassus. She'll help you make up for all that lost time.

original: Although I am flattered by your confidence in my abilities, teaching you is beyond my skill. You must go to the Craftsmen's Terrace in Darnassus, and speak with the night elf Ainethil. She can help you.
text: I'm flattered you think I'm that good, I really am. But teachin' you is beyond my skill. Go to the Craftsmen's Terrace in Darnassus, and talk to the night elf Ainethil. She can help you.

original:
Hey!  Adventurer!  Come here!

My raiders and I are about to attack the Silverwing Outpost to the west.  Our target is its leader, Duriel Moonfire.  Scouts report the outpost is defended heavily with sentinels and warriors.  The battle will be glorious!

Do you want to share in the glory, Adventurer, and aid us?  If so, then when it's over you can report our success to my superior, Ertog Ragetusk in Splintertree.

What do you say.  Are you with us?
text:
Hey! Adventurer! Get over here!

Me and my raiders are about to hit the Silverwing Outpost, to the west. Our target is its leader, Duriel Moonfire. Scouts say the place is crawlin' with sentinels and warriors. Heavily defended. You know what that means? It means this battle is gonna be glorious as hell!

You wanna share in that glory and help us out? Then when it's over, you report our success to my superior, Ertog Ragetusk, in Splintertree.

So what do you say? Are you with us, or not?

original:
Delgren has asked me to deliver messages and supplies to Sentinel Starbreeze in Auberdine, but I am loathe to leave on my own. Dangerous foes operate in the forest, and I do not wish to risk letting these supplies and information fall into the wrong hands.

If you and others could act as my guards, I could leave now. With your protection, I have no doubt that we can see these goods safely to Auberdine.
text:
Delgren asked me to deliver messages and supplies to Sentinel Starbreeze in Auberdine. Fine. But I ain't goin' alone. There's dangerous motherfuckers runnin' around this forest, and I'm not about to let these supplies and this information fall into the wrong hands.

Now, if you and some others act as my guards, I can leave right now. With your protection, I got no doubt we'll get these goods to Auberdine safe and sound.

original:
So Torek's attack was successful!  Well done, Adventurer.  Night elves are decent foes.  A little skinny, but strong and fierce!  I'm sure the battle was something to see...

And I hope you gained a scar or two!
text:
So Torek's attack worked! Hell yeah! Well done, Adventurer. Night elves make decent enemies. A little skinny, sure, but strong and fierce as hell! I bet that fight was somethin' to see...

And I hope you walked away with a scar or two!

original: Torek was sent on a mission against Silverwing Outpost. Was the attack successful?
text: Torek went out on a mission against Silverwing Outpost. So tell me. Did the attack succeed or not?

original:
Have you slain Ran yet, my friend?

Even the Night elves do not truly deserve his wrath. His hatred burns even brighter than my own, but his mind is no longer his own. He is a threat to all the natural creatures of this forest.
text:
Have you killed Ran yet, my friend?

Even the Night elves don't truly deserve his wrath. And believe me, I don't love them either. His hatred burns even hotter than my own, but his mind ain't his own no more. That crazy son of a bitch is a threat to every natural creature in this forest.

original: Have you found them? What did Anilia say? Where is she?
text: Did you find them? What did Anilia say? Where the hell is she?

original: Please, help me avenge Anilia's death.
text: Please. Help me avenge Anilia's death. Make those bastards pay.

original:
Most impressive, Adventurer... the claw of Sharptalon could not have been easy to get!  The Ashenvale Hunt goes well for you!

Sharptalon had long terrorized the peons from the lumber camps near its path as they tried to travel here to Splintertree Post.  No doubt once the word gets out that it was you who put down the beast, many rousing songs of your bravery will be heard at campfires and lumber mills across Ashenvale!
text:
Well, look at you. You actually did it. The claw of Sharptalon, right here in my hand, and I know damn well that wasn't easy to get. The Ashenvale Hunt is going good for you, adventurer!

That feathered son of a bitch terrorized the peons from the lumber camps for years. Every time they tried to travel along its path to Splintertree Post, there it was. Not anymore. Once word gets out that you put that beast down, they'll be singing your name at every goddamn campfire and lumber mill across Ashenvale!

original:
Ah, the paw of Ursangous!  Your skill is impressive, adventurer; he is credited with numerous kills.  The crescent on his paw is no doubt a sign that he was trained by the night elves that skulk about Ashenvale.  Ursangous is... was one of the mightiest bears you'd find in these parts.  To have bested such a creature is a testament to your will and resolve.

Your ancestors would be proud!
text:
The paw of Ursangous. Hell yes! That bear racked up more kills than I care to count, and you walked out there and ended him. You see that crescent on his paw? That's the mark of the night elves who skulk around Ashenvale. They trained that motherfucker.

Ursangous is... no. Was. Was one of the mightiest bears in these parts. And you bested him. That's will. That's resolve. That's a testament, adventurer.

Your ancestors would be proud as hell!

original:
A victory for Adventurer in the Ashenvale Hunt!  Well done - the head of Shadumbra is a fitting trophy to claim for such an impressive fight, no doubt.

Shadumbra's savagery was well known throughout the post here.  Any trip to the west, especially on foot trying to get out to the Zoram Strand, was wrought with danger because of this tiger.  Thanks to you, this danger has abated.
text:
A victory in the Ashenvale Hunt! Damn right! The head of Shadumbra is a fitting trophy for a fight like that, no doubt about it.

Everybody at this post knew how savage that tiger was. You wanted to go west, especially on foot out toward the Zoram Strand? You were taking your goddamn life in your hands. Thanks to you, that danger is over. Done. Finished.

original:
Welcome to the new frontier, Adventurer.  Ashenvale is a land of opportunity, one where a young adventurer like yourself is able to find boundless chances to prove their mettle.  Look around the outpost here, and be sure to travel out to the Zoram Strand, as the Horde has another outpost there as well.

Your presence here tells me that you've come to learn more about the hunt.  Listen close, and I will gladly share with you what you need to know.
text:
Welcome to the new frontier, adventurer. Ashenvale. Land of opportunity. A young fighter like you can find more chances to prove your mettle out here than you can shake a damn stick at. Look around this outpost, and make sure you travel out to the Zoram Strand, because the Horde has another outpost out there too.

Now, you showed up here, which tells me you want to learn about the hunt. So listen close. I'm gonna tell you what you need to know.

original:
Welcome to the new frontier, Adventurer.  Ashenvale is a land of opportunity, one where a young adventurer like yourself is able to find boundless chances to prove their mettle.  Look around the outpost here, and be sure to travel out to the Zoram Strand, as the Horde has another outpost there as well.

Your presence here tells me that you've come to learn more about the hunt.  Listen close, and I will gladly share with you what you need to know.
text:
Welcome to the new frontier, friend. This is Ashenvale, and it is a land of motherfuckin' opportunity. Somebody young and hungry like you? You'll find boundless chances out here to prove your mettle. Take a look around the outpost, and get yourself out to the Zoram Strand, too. The Horde's got another outpost there.

You came here for the hunt. I can see it on you. So shut up a second and listen close, and I'll share what you need to know.

original:
Welcome to the new frontier, Adventurer.  Ashenvale is a land of opportunity, one where a young adventurer like yourself is able to find boundless chances to prove their mettle.  Look around the outpost here, and be sure to travel out to the Zoram Strand, as the Horde has another outpost there as well.

Your presence here tells me that you've come to learn more about the hunt.  Listen close, and I will gladly share with you what you need to know.
text:
You made it to the new frontier, adventurer. Ashenvale. A land where a young hero can prove their mettle every damn day of the week, if they've got the guts for it. Look around this outpost, then travel out to the Zoram Strand. The Horde has another outpost out there as well.

And don't tell me you're just sightseeing. You came to learn about the hunt. Good. Listen close, and I'll gladly tell you what you need to know.

original:
There are three legendary creatures that make up the Ashenvale Hunt; you may seek them and test yourself against their cunning and might.  In the process, you will hopefully learn something about yourself.  The creatures are: the bear Ursangous, the nightsaber cat Shadumbra, and the hippogryph Sharptalon.

The creatures of the Ashenvale Hunt are powerful, and you may find that you'll need aid in bringing them down.  If you should best them, bring me proof of your deed.
text:
Three. There are three legendary creatures that make up the Ashenvale Hunt. You go out there, you seek them, and you test yourself against their cunning and their might. And maybe, just maybe, you learn something about yourself in the process.

Here they are. The bear, Ursangous. The nightsaber cat, Shadumbra. And the hippogryph, Sharptalon.

Now hear me. These creatures are powerful as hell. You might need some friends to bring them down, and there's no shame in that. You best them, you bring me proof of the deed.

original: Yes, mighty adventurer, I sensed your arrival.  I trust you have more news to report to me about your hunt?
text: Yes, mighty adventurer, I felt you coming a mile off. You got more news about your hunt for me, or what?

original: Ah - Adventurer - I was just thinking about you!  How goes your hunting?
text: Adventurer! I was just thinking about your ass. So tell me, how's the hunting going?

original: Greetings once again, Adventurer!  Have you come to show me proof of your hunt?
text: Well, damn, back again, adventurer! You come to show me proof of your hunt?

original: Do you hear the call of the hunt, adventurer?  You must listen closely, but the call comes from deep within you.  It comes from deep within all of us.
text: You hear that? The call of the hunt, adventurer. No, not out there. You gotta listen close, because that call comes from deep inside you. Deep inside all of us. Every last one.

original:
Adventurer, a longtime friend of mine is also aiding the Sentinels here in Ashenvale, but he has yet to return.

He had leads on finding an item that he thought could slow the furbolg attacks on our people--a rod created by a now-dead, evil wizard.

Before he left here, he mentioned seeking out a gem for the rod.

He mentioned the gem possibly being hidden at the shrine in Lake Falathim at the base of the mountain to the west. The gem was being held there before it was overrun.

Find my friend, Adventurer, please.
text:
Adventurer, listen to me. A longtime friend of mine is out there helping the Sentinels here in Ashenvale, and he has not come back. Not a word.

He had leads on something that could slow down these goddamn furbolg attacks on our people. A rod. Made by some evil wizard who's dead now, thank Elune.

Before he left, he said he was going after a gem for that rod. He thought it might be hidden at the shrine in Lake Falathim, at the base of the mountain to the west. The gem was kept there before the whole damn place got overrun.

Find my friend, adventurer. Please. I am asking you.

original:
You'll have to do the research yourself, but from what notes Teronis has made, it sounds like your next course of action is to find the other pieces of the rod Dartol created. I would start by heading to the moonwell east of Iris Lake. When you're ready, follow the road and turn north when you reach a small sitting area on your left.

A dryad there named Shael'dryn is better suited to guide you. Seek her out.

Keep the gem with you--Shael'dryn will need it if she's to help you recreate the rod.
text:
You're gonna have to do the research yourself, but from the notes Teronis made, your next move is to find the other pieces of the rod Dartol created. Start at the moonwell east of Iris Lake. When you're ready, follow the road, and when you hit a small sitting area on your left, you turn north. North!

There's a dryad there named Shael'dryn. She's better at guiding you through this shit than I am. Go find her.

And keep that gem on you, you hear me? Shael'dryn's gonna need it if she's gonna help you recreate the rod.

original:
Before you travel to the moonwell I have another task that will aid the people of Ashenvale if you would like to test your skills.

Along the road heading east before the Falfarren River, furbolgs have been attacking travelers. Their tortured minds feeding upon fear, and their appetites satiated by the blood of innocents.

Aid the Sentinels in protecting the lands by showing those monsters the same mercy they have shown our kind.

I believe their camps are south of the road... be careful.
text:
Before you head off to that moonwell, I've got another job, if you want to test your skills and help the people of Ashenvale.

Along the road heading east, before the Falfarren River, the furbolgs have been attacking travelers. Their twisted, tortured minds feed on fear. And their appetites? Satisfied by the blood of innocents. Sick bastards.

Help the Sentinels protect these lands. Show those monsters the exact same mercy they've shown our kind. Which is none.

I believe their camps are south of the road. Be careful out there, damn it.

original:
Alas, I'm not completely certain what he had in mind next.

If what he said was true about the rod's power, then it will allow you to take on another form altogether. Which form, I do not know.

Perhaps he meant to use its powers to get closer to the tainted furbolgs, but even the uncorrupted creatures would slaughter him were he not careful. Transformed by the rod, Dartol would have to speak to a furbolg who was safe from the effects of Fel Moss.

I would start your search southeast of Mystral Lake.
text:
Honestly? I'm not completely sure what he had planned next.

If he was right about the rod's power, it'll let you take on another form entirely. Which form? Hell if I know.

Maybe he meant to use it to get close to the tainted furbolgs. But even the uncorrupted ones would slaughter him if he wasn't careful. So, transformed by the rod, Dartol would've needed to talk to a furbolg who was safe from the effects of the Fel Moss. One who hasn't lost his goddamn mind.

Start your search southeast of Mystral Lake.

original:
Directly to the north of Astranaar are the Thistlefur furbolg. My scouts report that their numbers have grown greatly over the past few months. If they grow too great, they may find the courage to attack Astranaar directly.

Kill as many of their kind as you can, but bring me their chieftain's skull as proof that their efforts have been stifled... for now.

I shall remain here in Astranaar and await word from you. Elune be with you.
text:
Directly north of Astranaar, you've got the Thistlefur furbolg. My scouts say their numbers have exploded over the past few months. And if they get too big, they're gonna find the courage to come at Astranaar directly. That is not happening. Not on my watch.

Kill as many of those mangy sons of bitches as you can. But bring me their chieftain's skull, as proof that we shut their shit down... for now.

I'll be right here in Astranaar, waiting on your word. Elune be with you.

original:
Ah, a adventurer from Darkshore. Selarin has done well to send you here so quickly, Adventurer. I wish your trip here wasn't under such dire stress. Perhaps with your help we can improve matters.

I would start my visit by speaking to the other citizens of Astranaar. Some could surely use your aid.
text:
An adventurer from Darkshore. Selarin did good, sending you here this fast. I just wish your trip came under better circumstances, because things are dire as hell around here. Maybe with your help, we can fix that.

If I were you, I'd start by talking to the other citizens of Astranaar. Some of them could surely use a hand.

original:
This is terrible, Adventurer. Teronis is dead?!

The time for mourning will come, but for now we must focus our efforts. I shall send some of the Sentinels to recover Teronis' body as soon as possible.

You have Teronis' journal and the gem he was seeking. Do you think you're capable of completing his task? I would rest much better knowing his death was not in vain.
text:
No. No, no, no. Teronis is dead?!

Damn it. There'll be time to mourn him later. Right now we focus. I'm sending some of the Sentinels to recover Teronis' body as soon as possible.

You've got Teronis' journal, and you've got the gem he was after. So I'm asking you straight. Can you finish what he started? Because I would rest a whole hell of a lot better knowing he didn't die for nothing.

original: You have done well, Adventurer. Thank you.
text: Damn good work, adventurer. Thank you. Truly.

original:
You've recreated the rod Teronis had set out to find? That's wonderful to hear.

Teronis would be proud to see his quest is continuing even after his tragic passing.
text:
You recreated the rod? The one Teronis set out to find? Well, that's the best goddamn news I've heard all week.

Teronis would be proud, seeing his quest keep going even after his tragic passing.

original:
So, this is the skull of the fiercest furbolg threat in Ashenvale?

I am more than pleased with your abilities, Adventurer. The Sentinels cannot thank you enough. I hope we can rely on you again in the future to help our people.

I shall put this skull and Dartol's Rod in a place of reverence for others to see.

Teronis would be proud. Thank you again.
text:
So this is it. The skull of the fiercest furbolg threat in all of Ashenvale?

I am more than pleased with you, adventurer. The Sentinels can't thank you enough, and I mean that. I hope we can count on you again when our people need it, because they will.

I'm putting this skull, and Dartol's Rod, someplace of reverence, so everybody can see what was done here.

Teronis would be proud. Thank you, friend. Thank you.

original:
Well done, Adventurer.

We are under constant threat from the furbolg. Hopefully this will keep them at bay for a bit longer.
text:
Well done, adventurer.

Those furbolg bastards never stop coming at us. But this ought to keep them at bay a little while longer.

original: Ah, welcome back, Adventurer.
text: Ah, there you are. Welcome back, adventurer.

original:
Balthule's letter is dire. This Cult of the Dark Strand is a thorn in my side that must be removed. I have been dealing with some of the Dark Strand scum northeast of here at Ordil'Aran. One of their number possesses a soul gem that I believe holds the secret to the cult's power.

Bring it to me, and I will be able to decipher the secrets held within.
text:
Balthule's letter is dire. Dire! This Cult of the Dark Strand is a thorn in my side, and I am done with it. I have been dealing with some of that Dark Strand scum northeast of here, at Ordil'Aran. One of those bastards has a soul gem, and I believe it holds the secret to the whole cult's power.

You bring it to me. I'll crack that motherfucker open and read every secret inside.

original:
Ilkrud Magthrull. Yes, I have knowledge of him. He is a powerful orc warlock that makes his residence at the Fire Scar Shrine,  a place of great evil in southwestern Ashenvale.

He had been little more than an annoyance until now, and I had not dealt with him, but it seems that his time has come.
text:
Ilkrud Magthrull. Oh, I know that name. Powerful orc warlock, lives at the Fire Scar Shrine, a place of pure goddamn evil down in southwestern Ashenvale.

Until now he's been nothing but an annoyance, and I let him slide. That was a mistake. His time has come.

original:
The writing of the orcs is little better than the scribblings of a child. Many of my order scoffed when I chose to learn their tongue, but I have found it beneficial to gain further understanding of my enemies.

From Ilkrud's scribblings, it appears that Athrikus still possesses two soulgems, and they are being held in Night Run and Satyrnaar, satyr-held areas in northeast Ashenvale.

Be careful out there, adventurer, the satyrs' blood-soaked temples can be unsettling even for a seasoned adventurer such as yourself.
text:
Orc writing is barely better than a child's scribbles. Half my order laughed at me when I chose to learn their tongue. Well, who's laughing now? Know your enemy, damn it.

From Ilkrud's scribblings, Athrikus still has two soulgems. They're being held in Night Run and Satyrnaar, satyr-held areas in northeast Ashenvale.

And watch yourself, adventurer. Those satyrs' blood-soaked temples will mess with your head, even a seasoned killer like you.

original: Before confronting Athrikus, it would probably be wise for you to consult with Balthule. I have no doubt he has been vigilant in his watch of the Tower, and he may have information about recent developments.
text: Before you go stomping up to Athrikus, do yourself a favor and talk to Balthule. I guarantee he's been watching that Tower like a hawk, and he may know about whatever new hell has been happening there.

original:
If you don't mind my saying, you seem a bit well-equipped for a messenger, hm? I suppose Balthule wanted to be certain that his letter reached my hands. Let's see what he has to say...

This is disturbing news. When undead or demonic forces are found, I help the Sentinels destroy them.

At first I was unaccustomed to the manners of the night elves, but I have grown to respect them greatly as allies.
text:
If you don't mind me saying, you're a little heavily armed for a damn messenger, hm? I suppose Balthule wanted to be sure this letter actually got to me. Let's see what he has to say...

This is disturbing. Very disturbing. When undead or demonic filth shows its face, I help the Sentinels wipe it out.

I'll be honest, the night elves' ways threw me at first. But I've come to respect them greatly as allies. Good people. Dangerous people.

original: Hmm, some dark magic enchants this soulstone. Let's see what's trapped inside, shall we?
text: Hmm. Some dark magic enchants this soulstone. Nasty shit. Well, let's crack it open and see what's trapped inside, shall we?

original:
It was a grand thing you did today, adventurer. You should be quite proud of yourself for having faced down a warlock of such power.

Now, let's see what we can learn from Ilkrud's writings.
text:
That was a hell of a thing you did today, adventurer. You looked a warlock of that kind of power in the eye and you put him down. You should be damn proud.

Now. Let's see what we can learn from Ilkrud's writings.

original:
You have done well today, adventurer. The items we sent to aid Auberdine will be of immediate use in dealing with the dark threats that infest the forest.

Take these with my heartfelt thanks.
text:
You did good today, adventurer. Those items we sent to help Auberdine are going straight to work against the dark filth infesting this forest.

Take these, with my heartfelt thanks.

original:
I knew you would be up to the task, adventurer.

I sense great deeds before you, and that you will right many of the wrongs that plague our lands. Bear my blessings, adventurer, as well as this gift.
text:
I knew you'd be up to the task, adventurer. Never doubted it for a goddamn second.

I see great deeds in front of you. You're going to right a lot of the wrongs plaguing our lands. Carry my blessings with you, adventurer, and this gift as well.

original:
Perhaps the satyrs have been allowed to persist in the forest for too long. I will speak with Elissa about it when next I travel to Auberdine.

Nonetheless, with the soulgems destroyed, Athrikus' power will be greatly diminished. We must seize on this opportunity to eliminate him and his cult.
text:
Maybe we've let these satyrs fester in this forest for too damn long. I'll speak with Elissa about it next time I travel to Auberdine.

Either way, with those soulgems destroyed, Athrikus' power just got cut off at the knees. Now we seize this moment, and we wipe out him and his whole cult.

original: You have some business with me, adventurer?
text: You got some business with me, adventurer?

original:
Adventurer, you have slain all three beasts that comprise the Ashenvale Hunt.  You have brought me adequate proof of their demise; there is no question of your strength and tenacity.  The blood of a hunter streaks through your veins, and you should be commended!

Please, accept this bauble as a sign of congratulations on your mighty deeds done in Ashenvale for the Horde today.  May your ancestors watch over you!
text:
Adventurer, you did it. All three beasts of the Ashenvale Hunt, dead. Every last one. And you brought me proof enough of their demise. Nobody can question your strength or your tenacity now. Nobody! The blood of a hunter runs hot through your veins, and you deserve to be commended for it!

Here. Take this bauble, as my congratulations for the mighty deeds you did in Ashenvale for the Horde today. May your ancestors watch over you!

original: Have you acquired that soul gem?
text: Well? You get me that soul gem or not?

original:
Take this divining scroll--it can determine the creator of these elementals. But you will need something from them to use as a reagent to focus scroll's magic--their bracers should do nicely.

A few intact bracers from the creatures should be enough. The other bracers will be useless for our purposes, but they may be worth something to a merchant if you wish to sell them. Once you have the intact bracers attempt to use the scroll. Return to me with the results and we shall proceed from there.
text:
Take this divining scroll. It can tell us who the hell created these elementals. But the scroll needs something from them to focus its magic, a reagent, and their bracers will do just fine.

A few intact bracers off those creatures ought to be enough. The rest of the bracers are useless to us, but some merchant might pay you for the junk if you want to sell it. Once you've got intact bracers, use the scroll. Then you bring the results back to me, and we figure out who's behind this shit.

original:
There's only one undead mage in the Barrens capable of defiling this many water elementals. He's also the only one foolish enough to try. Sarilus Foulborne is probably sitting at the top of Dreadmist Peak, laughing at me.

adventurer, you must go into enemy territory and destroy this miscreant. I have had enough of his idiocy and we must show him what happens to those who annoy the Sentinels.

Destroy him and bring me his head. Be wary though, the Horde may be watching for you.
text:
There is only one undead mage in the Barrens with the power to defile this many water elementals. And he's the only one dumb enough to try it. Sarilus Foulborne. That smug son of a bitch is probably sitting on top of Dreadmist Peak right now, laughing at me.

Adventurer, you are going into enemy territory, and you are going to destroy this miscreant. I have had enough of his goddamn idiocy. We are going to show him exactly what happens to people who annoy the Sentinels.

Kill him. Bring me his head. And watch your back, because the Horde may be watching for you.

original: Well done, Adventurer, this should give us the information we need to have the culprit discovered. How would you feel about taking out the mage who fills our pools with corrupt elementals? The corruption of Ashenvale and beyond makes my stomach turn on its own--to have a wizard actively attempting to destroy it further sickens me to no end. We shall make him pay.
text:
